name: @kitora/form
description: Kitora's form engine: a framework-free core, React bindings, the field catalog, auto forms, data sources, server validation, Yjs collaboration and devtools.

exports.name: AUTO_FORM_LABELS
exports.description: Labels for the array controls (override per form through `labels`).

exports.name: AutoField
exports.description: Render one field of the enclosing AutoForm's definition by path, so a hand-written layout can place generated fields. A missing path renders an inline alert rather than nothing, so a typo is visible.

props.name: name
props.description: Absolute path of the field in the definition, such as `address.city`.

exports.name: AutoForm
exports.description: Render a styled, validated form from a definition (or, deprecated, a field manifest).

props.name: def
props.description: The definition to render (from `defineForm`).

props.name: fields
props.description: Field manifest to render when no `def` is given.
props.deprecated: the older field manifest; converted with `fromManifest`. Pass `def` instead.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Called when the form submits and passes validation, with the output values.

props.name: widgets
props.description: Widget registry that maps each field `type` to its component.

props.name: onStore
props.description: Receives the form store once (tests, external controls).

props.name: cols
props.description: Grid columns for the top-level layout.

props.name: submitLabel
props.description: Label of the submit button (and of the wizard's last-step button).

props.name: hideSubmit
props.description: Hide the built-in submit button (e.g. when an external action bar submits).

props.name: children
props.description: Extra content rendered after the generated fields, above the submit button.

props.name: messages
props.description:
The message catalog for every built-in text — required, rule defaults,
array limits, and the React chrome (`Add`, `Remove`, `Saving…`). Default
English. `createTranslator(MESSAGE_BUNDLES.de)` switches locale;
`.with({ required: "…" })` rewords single keys.

props.name: plugins
props.description: Plugins to install on the store (persist, transport, tab sync…).

props.name: defaultValues
props.description: The form's initial values; also its first clean baseline.

props.name: lockPaths
props.description:
Optimistic-lock token paths (a `version`, an `etag` field). A dirty
serialize (`serialize({ mode: "dirty" })`, a PATCH) always carries them,
although the person never edits them, so the server can reject a stale
write with 409/412 (the conflict return path; H28 force-include).

props.name: context
props.description:
G2 — app context the rules read with `c.ctx("plan")` / `e.ctx("user.role")`:
permissions, plan, "account linked", a feature flag. JSON only, so a
definition that reads it stays serializable. It is NOT form data: never in
`getValues`/`serialize`, never dirty, not in history. Change it with
`setContext` (React: `useForm({ context })` re-applies it on every render).

props.name: registry
props.description:
Named operators, validators, effects and codecs the model references.
Default: `catalogRegistry()` — the catalog fields' own names (`luhn`,
`notExpired`, `matrixRows`, `timeRange`, card codecs). Extend it rather than
starting from `createRegistry()` when a form also uses catalog fields.

props.name: loaders
props.description: Named async loaders for `options: { resource }`.

props.name: autosave
props.description: Save each field on its own (blur or debounced change); status in `FieldRecord.save`.

props.name: schema
props.description: A Standard Schema the whole value is validated against.

props.name: schemaReports
props.description: How completely `schema` reports issues; see {@link SCHEMA_REPORTS}. Default `"auto"`.

props.name: schemaLibraryOptions
props.description:
Vendor settings passed on every schema call as Standard Schema
`validate(value, { libraryOptions })` — e.g. `{ abortEarly: false }` asks a
vendor that reads it (Valibot, Yup adapters) for every issue, which makes
`schemaReports: "all"` true. Vendors that ignore it are unaffected.

props.name: schemaScopes
props.description:
H9 — sub-schemas for big forms, keyed by a path pattern (`*` = any one
segment): `{ "rows.*": rowSchema }`. A per-change run whose changed path
falls under a pattern validates ONLY that subtree with its sub-schema
(issues re-rooted under it) instead of the whole `schema`, so a keystroke in
row 512 of 1,000 costs one row. Cross-field refinements of the whole
`schema` then run on submit, `validate()` and the debounced whole run below.
Standard Schema has no "validate this path" call, so the sub-schema is the
author's to give (Zod `rowSchema`, `schema.shape.rows.element`, a JSON
Schema fragment).

props.name: schemaDebounceMs
props.description:
H9 — how per-change runs of the whole `schema` are spaced. A number: always
debounce by that many ms (field rules still answer at once; the schema's
issues keep showing until its next run). Default `"auto"`: debounce by
{@link SCHEMA_DEBOUNCE_MS} only once one whole run took longer than
{@link SLOW_SCHEMA_MS} (a big form), otherwise run on every change. `0`
never debounces.

props.name: toSubmit
props.description: Authoritative payload transform (rename/restructure/coerce). Payload type = its return (C5).

props.name: validateOn
props.description: When a field is first validated: on `change`, `blur`, `submit` or `mount`.

props.name: revalidateOn
props.description: When a field already in error is validated again.

props.name: csrf
props.description:
CSRF token lifecycle: when a submit fails with an HTTP 403
(`SubmitError.status`), `refresh` fetches a fresh token, the store writes
it to `path` (a clean, non-dirty write) and resubmits ONCE with the new
payload. A second 403, or a refresh that fails, ends in `error` with every
value kept. Without it a 403 is an ordinary error.

exports.name: fromManifest
exports.description: Convert a manifest to a definition plus its ReactNode presentation. Logs a deprecation (AutoForm calls it once per mount).
exports.signature: <T>(fields: readonly FieldDescriptor[]) => { def: FormDef<T>; presentation: Presentation; }

exports.name: Presentation

exports.name: WIDGET_VALUE_TYPES
exports.description:
Value kind a widget edits (documentation + tooling; composites use it for

core's {@link VALUE_KINDS}: the React-free decoder needs the same vocabulary.

exports.name: WidgetEntry
exports.description: One widget in a {@link WidgetRegistry}: the field `type` it handles, its component and the kind of value it edits.

exports.name: WidgetProps
exports.description: What a widget receives: the bound path, its node, and the node's presentation already resolved.

props.name: props

props.name: span
props.description: Grid columns the field spans in the form layout.

exports.name: WidgetRegistry
exports.description: Immutable map from field `type` to widget; `extend` returns a new registry with more widgets.

exports.name: WidgetValueType
exports.description: One of {@link WIDGET_VALUE_TYPES}: the kind of value a widget edits.

exports.name: defaultWidgets
exports.description:
Every shipped field, by model type. Types whose field needs code a JSON

exports.name: bindYjs
exports.description: Bind `store` to `opts.doc`. Returns the live binding; `destroy()` unbinds.

exports.name: DEFAULT_ROOT
exports.description: Default name of the doc's root Y.Map that holds the form's values.

exports.name: HISTORY_KINDS
exports.description: The `meta.history` values the store's undo / redo change events carry.

exports.name: UNDO_CAPTURE_MS
exports.description: Default Y.UndoManager capture window (ms): keystrokes closer than this undo as one step.

exports.name: CollabStore
exports.description: The store surface the binding needs (a slice of the plugin surface); `FormStore<T>` is assignable.

exports.name: TextDelta
exports.description: One Y.Text change as a Yjs delta (retain / insert / delete runs).

exports.name: YjsBinding
exports.description: A live store ↔ Y.Doc binding: the doc, its root map, an undo stack of this client's edits only, and `destroy`.

exports.name: YjsBindingOptions
exports.description: Options for `bindYjs`: the shared doc and root map name, the text policy, which paths stay local, and the sync gate.

exports.name: COLLAB_CHANNEL_PREFIX
exports.description: Prefix of the BroadcastChannel names, so a collab room never collides with an app's own channel.

exports.name: createYProvider
exports.description: Connect `doc` (and its presence) to every peer on the transport.

exports.name: isYMessage
exports.description: Type guard for what arrives: anything else (another app's message, a forged one) is ignored.

exports.name: SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS
exports.description: How long a joiner waits for a peer's `sync2` before treating itself as alone (ms).

exports.name: Y_MESSAGE_KINDS
exports.description: Wire message kinds. Canonical list.

exports.name: YMessage
exports.description: One message on the transport (structured-cloned; Uint8Array survives a BroadcastChannel).

exports.name: YMessageKind
exports.description: One of {@link Y_MESSAGE_KINDS}: the kind of a wire message.

exports.name: YProvider
exports.description: A transport-agnostic Yjs provider: keeps the doc and awareness in sync with peers on one channel.

exports.name: YProviderOptions
exports.description: Options for `createYProvider`: the transport (or a room for the default BroadcastChannel) and the sync timeout.

exports.name: bindPresence
exports.description:
Publish `user` and track the focused field from the store's focus / blur
events. Returns the unbind, which clears this client's focus (the provider's
`destroy` removes the whole presence).
exports.signature: (store: Pick<PluginStore, "onEvent">, awareness: Awareness, user: CollabUser) => () => void

exports.name: FALLBACK_COLOR
exports.description: Colour used when a peer publishes something that is not a hex colour.

exports.name: MAX_NAME_LENGTH
exports.description: Longest display name kept (a peer could publish a novel).

exports.name: parsePeer
exports.description: Parse one awareness state; null when it carries no usable user.
exports.signature: (clientId: number, state: unknown, selfId: number) => Peer | null

exports.name: PRESENCE_KEYS
exports.description: Keys of the awareness state this module owns. Canonical list.

exports.name: readPeers
exports.description: Every client with a user in `awareness`, self first then by client id (stable order for avatars).

exports.name: safeColor
exports.description: A safe colour for CSS: the hex literal itself, else the fallback.

exports.name: CollabUser
exports.description: Who a client is, as shown to the others.

exports.name: Peer
exports.description: One client in the room, as read from awareness.

exports.name: caretKeeper
exports.description:
Keep the caret of the focused input in `scope` where the person put it when
a remote text change lands in that field: the store re-renders the input
with the merged value (which would move the caret to the end), then the
selection is restored, shifted by the remote delta, on the next frame.

exports.name: COLLAB_SCOPE_ATTR
exports.description: Attribute that marks one collaborative form's DOM subtree (focus rings and the caret keeper look inside it).

exports.name: PresenceRings
exports.description:
A coloured ring on every field another person has focused, inside `scope`.
Rendered as a scoped stylesheet keyed by the input's `name`, so no field
component needs to know about collaboration. Colours and paths come from
peers and are validated (hex only, field-name characters only).

props.name: peers
props.description: Everyone in the session; the local peer and peers with no focused field are skipped.

props.name: scope
props.description: The collab scope id the rings are limited to (the value of the scope attribute on the form's wrapper).

exports.name: toCollabPeers
exports.description:
The form's peers in `@kitora/collab`'s `Peer` shape, so collab's presence views
(`PresenceAvatars`, `PresenceAvatar`, …) draw them: the one avatar stack in the kits.
A form peer publishes no activity, so every peer is `active`; the focused field rides
in `custom` (`{ focus, focusLabel }`) for a host that shows where each person is.
exports.signature: (peers: readonly Peer[], labels?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>) => CollabPeer<FormPeerFocus>[]

exports.name: transformIndex
exports.description:
Where an index lands after a Yjs text delta. Inserts BEFORE it push it right,
deletes before it pull it left. An insert exactly AT the index does not move
it: two people typing at the same spot each keep their own run contiguous
(yours stays left of theirs) instead of interleaving letter by letter.

exports.name: usePeers
exports.description: Subscribe to the room's presence. Empty without an awareness (not connected yet).

exports.name: useYjsForm
exports.description:
Join `opts.room` with `form`: a Y.Doc, the BroadcastChannel provider (or
`opts.transport`), the store binding and presence, all torn down on unmount.

exports.name: FormPeerFocus
exports.description: What a form adds to a collab peer: the field path it has focused and that field's label.

exports.name: UseYjsForm
exports.description: What `useYjsForm` returns: the session once synced, the other people present, and the scope props for presence UI.

exports.name: UseYjsFormOptions
exports.description: Options for `useYjsForm`: the room, who this client is, the text policy and an optional transport factory.

exports.name: YjsFormSession
exports.description: A live session; null until the effect has connected.

exports.name: ANY_SEGMENT
exports.description: Wildcard segment in a {@link TextOption} pattern.

exports.name: textPolicy
exports.description: Build a {@link TextPolicy} from the `text` option (no option = no string is text).

exports.name: TextOption
exports.description:
The `text` option: a predicate, or path patterns where a `*` segment matches
any key or index (`["title", "body", "items.*.note"]`).

exports.name: TextPolicy
exports.description: Decides which string paths are collaborative text (Y.Text). Receives the concrete path (`"items.0.note"`).

exports.name: ApplyExternalOpts
exports.description: Options of `applyExternal`, the write path for values from outside the form (prefill, host undo, agents).

exports.name: AsyncLoader
exports.description: Loads options/value from `parent` (the dep values). `signal` cancels stale runs.

exports.name: ChangeOrigin
exports.description: Where a value mutation originated. onChange/analytics emit only for 'user'.

exports.name: EmptyPolicy
exports.description:
How an EMPTY value (`""`, `null`, `undefined`, `[]` — `isEmptyValue`) of a field
leaves the form in `serialize()` / submit (H28), whatever the control stored:
- `keep` (default) — as stored
- `omit` — key removed (a PATCH then leaves the server's value alone)
- `null` — explicit null (a PATCH clears the server's value)
- `undefined` — key present with `undefined` (dropped by JSON, kept by an in-process handler)
- `empty-string` — `""` (a backend whose column is NOT NULL text)

exports.name: FieldKind
exports.description: Field-kind presets over the 4 transport axes.

exports.name: FieldMeta
exports.description: Per-path registration metadata. Expanded in later phases (parse/format/sensitive/...).

exports.name: FieldRecord
exports.description:
Per-path field state. MUST be referentially stable across reads with no
mutation between them (the ref-stability invariant) or `useSyncExternalStore` infinite-loops.
The store caches one record per path and only swaps its reference when a
member actually changes.

exports.name: FormEvent
exports.description:
An instrumentation event, a discriminated union on `type`.
Sensitive values are never included. Shapes:
- `change` — a value changed; `origin` says who; `array` for structural array ops
- `focus` / `blur` — a field's control gained / lost focus (`path` set)
- `validate` — a validation pass settled; `scope` when partial, `valid` its verdict
- `status` — submit status changed; `status` is the new one
- `step` — a wizard moved from step `from` to step `to`
- `submit` — a submit started
- `reset` / `commit` — values replaced / the dirty baseline moved
(one union member per type, so `Extract<FormEvent, { type: K }>` narrows every K)
- `errors` — server errors were set or cleared; `paths` lists them
- `error` — a runtime model error (`kind`, `message`, `chain`)
- `abandon` — the page was left while dirty and unsubmitted; `lastPath` the last field touched
- `leave` — the form is being left (gap F: `<Form>` unmounted, or the host said so); `reason` why, `dirty` whether the values differ from the baseline
- `load` — an async load of the form's data changed state; `status` is the new one
- `work` — tracked field work (an upload, H29) started or settled at `path`; `pending` is the form-wide count now in flight

exports.name: FormEventInput
exports.description: An event as emitted, before the bus stamps `ts`.

exports.name: FormEventOf
exports.description: The event of one type, e.g. `FormEventOf<"change">`.

exports.name: FormEventType
exports.description: An event-bus event kind (see {@link FORM_EVENT_TYPES}).

exports.name: FormLoader
exports.description: A data loader: gets an AbortSignal (aborted when a newer load starts or the load is cancelled).

exports.name: Issue
exports.description: A validation issue with a normalized (canonical dot-index) path. "" = form-level.

exports.name: LeaveReason
exports.description: Why a form is being left (see {@link LEAVE_REASONS}).

exports.name: LoadState
exports.description: {@link LoadStatus} plus the failure of an `error` load (whatever the loader rejected with).

props.name: status
props.description: Where the load stands.

props.name: error
props.description: What the loader rejected with, when `status` is `error`.

exports.name: LoadStatus
exports.description: Where loading a record into the form stands (see {@link LOAD_STATUSES}).

exports.name: Listener
exports.description: A change listener with no arguments.

exports.name: PathSegment
exports.description: One segment of a parsed path: a key or an array index.

exports.name: ResetOpts
exports.description: Options of `reset`: what to keep from the current state.

exports.name: ResourceState
exports.description: State of an async resource (K8): dependent options or a loaded value.

props.name: loading
props.description: Whether a load is in flight.

props.name: error
props.description: The message of the last failed load.

props.name: options
props.description: Options the loader returned.

props.name: value
props.description: Value the loader returned.

exports.name: Sensitivity
exports.description: Classification for fields holding regulated data. Drives redaction.

exports.name: ServerIssue
exports.description: A server-side validation error (e.g. a 422 response), path in canonical or vendor form.

exports.name: SubmitStatus
exports.description: A submit lifecycle status (see {@link SUBMIT_STATUSES}).

exports.name: Trigger
exports.description: When validation fires. `validateOn` = first-surface; `revalidateOn` = after a field is already in error (H1).

exports.name: Unsubscribe
exports.description: Removes the listener it was returned for.

exports.name: ValidationResult
exports.description: Result of a validation run: whether it passed and the issues found.

exports.name: Capabilities
exports.description: Capability providers a plugin can supply: draft storage and the submit transport.

exports.name: Plugin
exports.description: A form plugin: provides capabilities, observes store events and transforms state on its way in or out.

exports.name: PluginStore
exports.description:
The minimal store surface a plugin's `setup` receives. Defined structurally (not
`FormStore<T>`) so a concrete `FormStore<Invoice>` is assignable without generic
variance friction.

exports.name: StorageCapability
exports.description: Persistence backend (autosave/draft). Sensitivity-aware persistence is layered on top.

exports.name: TransportCapability
exports.description: How a submit payload leaves the client (REST/GraphQL/server-action/iframe).

exports.name: BUSY_STATUSES
exports.description: Statuses during which a submit is in flight (re-entrant submits are ignored, `Form.Submit` is busy).

exports.name: FORM_EVENT_TYPES
exports.description:
Event-bus event kinds: every mutation that can change a
form-level aggregate (status, issues, dirtiness) emits one, because the
form-level React hooks re-read on events. Canonical list: {@link FORM_EVENT_TYPES}.

exports.name: LEAVE_REASONS
exports.description:
Why a form is being left (gap F), the `reason` of a `leave` event. Closed set:
- `unmount` — `<Form>` unmounted (in-app navigation; React calls it, once even under StrictMode)
- `pagehide` — the document is going away; a host that wants a draft on tab close calls `store.leave("pagehide")` itself, the engine never does

exports.name: LOAD_STATUSES
exports.description:
State of loading a record into a form (`useForm({ load })`). Separate
from the submit status: a form can be loading while idle, or loaded and
submitting. `idle` = nothing loading (never loaded, or cancelled).

exports.name: REQUIRED_MESSAGE
exports.description:
English message for a failed `required` rule (the catalog's `required` key; a
store with `messages` uses its own locale). Override per field by passing a
string as `required`.

exports.name: SUBMIT_STATUSES
exports.description:
Submit lifecycle: `idle → validating → submitting → success | error | conflict`,
or `validating → invalid` when client validation blocks ("you have
a typo" is not "the server said no"). Canonical list: {@link SUBMIT_STATUSES}.

exports.name: analytics
exports.description: Forwards every instrumentation event to a sink (analytics / telemetry).

exports.name: devtools
exports.description: Records events + changes into in-memory buffers for inspection/debugging.

exports.name: DRAFT_DISCARD_REASONS
exports.description:
Why a stored draft was thrown away instead of restored (L7). Closed set:
- `futureVersion` — written by a NEWER build than this one (a rolled-back deploy, a second tab on the new version); this build cannot know its shape
- `noMigration` — older, but the `migrations` chain has no step for one of the versions in between (a legacy unversioned draft is version 0)
- `migrationFailed` — a step threw or returned `null` (the draft did not have the shape that step expects)

exports.name: LEGACY_DRAFT_VERSION
exports.description: Version a legacy draft (a bare value tree saved before drafts were versioned) is treated as.

exports.name: memoryStorage
exports.description: In-memory storage driver (tests / SSR-neutral default).

exports.name: persist
exports.description:
Autosave/draft: restores a saved draft on setup (silently), then saves the
value tree after edits. Sensitivity-aware: sensitive (no-persist) fields are dropped
from the saved draft, so PII/PCI never lands in storage.

Lifecycle (L7):
- saves on `change` and `reset` events, debounced by `debounceMs`, when `saveIf` allows;
- a successful submit cancels any pending save and CLEARS the draft, so the
  next visit does not resurrect already-submitted data; a failed submit keeps it;
- drafts are stored as {@link PersistedDraft}; an older one runs through the
  `migrations` chain, and one that cannot be upgraded is cleared and reported
  (`onDiscard` + `console.warn`) — never applied to a form whose shape changed, never a crash;
- teardown (`store.destroy()`) flushes a pending save.
An async `storage.load()` is applied when it resolves, keeping fields the
user already edited.

exports.name: PERSIST_DEBOUNCE_MS
exports.description: Default quiet period before a draft is written (ms). Long enough to coalesce a typing burst into one storage write.

exports.name: PERSIST_DRAFT_VERSION
exports.description: Default draft schema version. Bump it (or pass `version`) when the form's value shape changes.

exports.name: readDraft
exports.description:
Bring a stored draft to `version` (pure; never throws). The chain runs one
step per version; any gap, failure or future version is a discard.
exports.signature: (saved: unknown, version: number, opts?: Pick<PersistOptions, "migrations" | "migrate">) => DraftRead

exports.name: saveOnLeave
exports.description:
Gap F — save a server draft when the form is left (`<Form>` unmounts, or the
host calls `store.leave(reason)`). Built only on the `leave` event; the
kernel decides nothing about drafts. Which keys go and how empties are
stripped is the app's mapping in `save`, never a plugin policy.

`T` is the values type of the form this plugin is passed to (`useForm<T>({ plugins })`).

exports.name: transport
exports.description: Submit transport: how the payload leaves the client.

exports.name: DevtoolsPlugin
exports.description: The plugin {@link devtools} returns, with the buffers it records into.

exports.name: DraftDiscard
exports.description: Reported to `onDiscard` (and logged) when a draft is not restored. `fromVersion` 0 = a legacy unversioned draft.

exports.name: DraftDiscardReason
exports.description: Why a stored draft was discarded (see {@link DRAFT_DISCARD_REASONS}).

exports.name: DraftMigration
exports.description: One upgrade step: the draft's values at version N in, the values at N + 1 out (`null` = not upgradeable).

exports.name: LeaveContext
exports.description: What `saveOnLeave`'s `when` and `save` receive when the form is left.

exports.name: PersistedDraft
exports.description: What `persist` writes to storage: the value tree tagged with the draft schema version.

exports.name: PersistOptions
exports.description: Options of the `persist` plugin: where drafts are stored, how often they save and how old drafts are upgraded.

exports.name: SaveOnLeaveOptions
exports.description: `saveOnLeave()` options: when a leave should save, and the fire-and-forget save itself.

exports.name: broadcastSyncChannel
exports.description: A {@link SyncChannel} over a BroadcastChannel named `name`, or null where BroadcastChannel does not exist (SSR, old browsers). Shared by tab sync and the collab provider.

exports.name: connectTabSync
exports.description:
Connect one form store to the other tabs of the same document. React apps
call {@link useTabSync } (it connects in an effect and disconnects on
unmount); elsewhere use the {@link tabSync} plugin or call this directly.

exports.name: createLeaderGate
exports.description: Create a {@link LeaderGate}; pass it to `useTabSync(form, { gate })`.

exports.name: TAB_SYNC_MESSAGE_KINDS
exports.description: Wire message kinds. `patch` = one field; `state` = the whole value tree (batch, undo, catch-up); `hello` = a tab joined.

exports.name: TAB_SYNC_PREFIX
exports.description: Prefix of the BroadcastChannel and Web Lock names, so a form's sync never collides with the app's own channels.

exports.name: tabSync
exports.description:
Multi-tab sync as a store plugin (non-React hosts). In React prefer
`useTabSync(form, opts)`: StrictMode creates a throwaway twin store whose
plugins are never torn down.

exports.name: LeaderGate
exports.description:
A stable "am I the leader?" function to hand to `persist({ saveIf })` BEFORE
the sync connects (in React the form, and so its plugins, exist before the
effect that connects the tabs). Unbound it answers true: a lone tab leads.

exports.name: SyncChannel
exports.description:
The transport a sync connection talks through (default: a BroadcastChannel;
inject a fake in tests, or another transport such as a SharedWorker port).
`send` structured-clones to every OTHER member; `listen` replaces the
handler of incoming data.

exports.name: SyncLocks
exports.description: The Web Locks surface used for leader election (`navigator.locks`).

exports.name: TabSyncHandle
exports.description: A live connection; `disconnect()` closes the channel and releases leadership.

exports.name: TabSyncMessage
exports.description: One message on the channel (structured-cloned, so values must be cloneable — files are not sent).

exports.name: TabSyncMessageKind
exports.description: A tab-sync wire message kind (see {@link TAB_SYNC_MESSAGE_KINDS}).

exports.name: TabSyncOptions
exports.description: Options of the `tabSync` plugin: the shared name and the channel and lock factories.

exports.name: TabSyncPatch
exports.description: The incoming patch `accept` decides on.

exports.name: TabSyncPlugin
exports.description: The {@link tabSync} plugin: `isLeader` is true while any store it is set up on leads (pass it to `persist({ saveIf })`).

exports.name: deepEqual
exports.description: Structural deep equality (used for dirty/baseline diffing).

exports.name: deleteIn
exports.description: Immutably remove the value at a path (clones along the spine). Used to strip local/derived keys at serialize.

exports.name: getIn
exports.description: Read the value at a path; returns undefined for any missing intermediate node.

exports.name: isSafePath
exports.description: True when no segment of `path` is in {@link UNSAFE_PATH_SEGMENTS}.

exports.name: normalizePath
exports.description: `items[0].qty` / `items['k']` → canonical dot-index `items.0.qty` / `items.k`.

exports.name: parsePath
exports.description: Parse a path into compiled segments (numeric segments become numbers). Cached.

exports.name: setIn
exports.description:
Immutable set with STRUCTURAL SHARING: only nodes along the changed path get
new references; siblings keep identity so selectors stay cheap. Auto-vivifies
missing intermediates (array when the next segment is numeric, else object).
exports.signature: <T>(obj: T, path: string | ReadonlyArray<PathSegment>, value: unknown) => T

exports.name: UNSAFE_PATH_SEGMENTS
exports.description:
Segments that would reach an object's prototype chain. Any path that crosses
a trust boundary (a posted form, a message from another tab) is checked with
{@link isSafePath} before it is written: `setIn(obj, "__proto__.x", 1)`
would pollute every object in the realm.

exports.name: path
exports.description:
Escape hatch for dynamic or beyond-ceiling paths: asserts a runtime string is
a valid `FieldPath<T>` so it can pass the typed store API. Use sparingly — it
bypasses static path checking. The supported fully-typed array path is the
`<FieldArray.Row>` scoped API (form-react), not interpolated strings.

exports.name: FieldPath
exports.description: Every valid dotted path of `T` (depth-limited).

exports.name: FieldValue
exports.description: The value type at path `P` of `T` (preserves |undefined / |null exactly).

exports.name: Primitive
exports.description: Leaf types we never descend into.

exports.name: inScope
exports.description: Is `path` within the validation `scope` prefix? (subset-by-prefix, K4)

exports.name: normalizeIssuePath
toIssues
exports.description: Map raw Standard Schema issues to engine `Issue`s with normalized paths.

exports.name: COLLECT_ALL_VENDORS
exports.description:
`~standard.vendor` names whose DEFAULT mode reports every issue. A schema of
one of these configured to abort early (Valibot `abortEarly: true`) needs
`schemaReports: "first"` — the vendor name cannot tell.

exports.name: createFormStore
exports.description:
Create the React-free form store: values, field records, the model runtime
(rules, derived values, effects), arrays with row ids, history, submit and the
plugin/event pipeline. Every adapter (React, AutoForm, tests) drives one of these.

Invariant: one store per form instance; `destroy()` releases plugins, autosave
and listeners, and a destroyed store must not be reused.
exports.typeParameters: <T extends object, TOut = T, TResult = unknown>
exports.signature: <T extends object, TOut = T, TResult = unknown>(config: CreateFormStoreConfig<T, TOut>) => FormStore<T, TOut, TResult>

exports.name: ISSUE_SOURCES
exports.description: Where an issue came from (devtools' validation tracer). Canonical list.

exports.name: matchScope
exports.description: The concrete prefix of `path` that `pattern` (`rows.*`, `*` = one segment) matches, or undefined.

exports.name: MAX_ABORT_EARLY_PROBES
exports.description:
Upper bound of probe runs per validation in `first` mode (one per kept
error). Past it the remaining errors are kept as they are: never dropped
unproven, at the cost of possibly showing a fixed error until the next run.

exports.name: REMOVE_BLOCKED_EVENT_KIND
exports.description: `kind` of the `error` event emitted when a guard blocks a remove (`message` is the reason, `path` the array).

exports.name: REMOVE_MISSING_REASON
exports.description: Reason reported when `remove` targets a row that does not exist (an old id, an index out of range).

exports.name: SCHEMA_DEBOUNCE_MS
exports.description: H9 — the debounce of per-change whole-schema runs on a big form (ms).

exports.name: SCHEMA_REPORTS
exports.description:
How completely the `schema` vendor reports issues (audit H11). Canonical list.
- `all` — every failing path in one result (Zod, ArkType, Valibot by default):
  a path the result does not mention is valid.
- `first` — the vendor may stop at the first failure (Valibot `abortEarly`,
  Yup's default, many custom vendors): a silent path is UNKNOWN, so an error
  it already has is kept unless a probe run proves it fixed.
- `auto` (default) — `all` for {@link COLLECT_ALL_VENDORS}; `first` for any
  other vendor until one result names two paths at once, which proves it collects.

exports.name: SLOW_SCHEMA_MS
exports.description: H9 — a whole-schema run slower than this (ms) marks the form big: per-change runs debounce. About half a 60 fps frame.

exports.name: defaultReferenceMessage
exports.description: Default block message (see {@link ReferenceGuardOptions.message}).
exports.signature: ({ label, count, noun }: { label: string; count: number; noun: string; }) => string

exports.name: REFERENCE_ACTIONS
exports.description: What happens to referencing rows when a referenced row is removed.

exports.name: referenceGuard
exports.description:
A {@link RemoveGuard} that keeps references between arrays consistent. The
row's id is read from `idKey`; a row with no id is never referenced.

exports.name: DEFAULT_HONEYPOT_NAME
exports.description: Name of the hidden trap input when none is given: innocuous-looking, so bots fill it.

exports.name: DEFAULT_MIN_FILL_MS
exports.description: Minimum plausible fill time when none is given, ms: a sub-second submit is almost always a bot.

exports.name: INTEGRITY_REASONS
exports.description: Why a submit was refused as likely automated; canonical list.

exports.name: judgeTraps
exports.description:
The traps' verdict: `undefined` lets the submit through, a reason refuses it.
The honeypot wins over timing (a filled trap is the stronger signal).
Whitespace in the trap counts as empty (some autofill writes a space).
exports.signature: ({ trapValue, elapsedMs, minFillMs }: TrapInput) => IntegrityReason | undefined

exports.name: IntegrityReason
exports.description: Why a submit was refused as likely bot traffic (see {@link INTEGRITY_REASONS}).

exports.name: TrapInput
exports.description: What `judgeTraps` weighs: the honeypot value, the fill time and the minimum plausible fill time.

exports.name: ReferenceAction
exports.description: What removing a referenced row does to rows that reference it: `block` it, `cascade` the removal, or `nullify` their keys.

exports.name: ReferenceGuardOptions
exports.description: Options of a reference guard: which arrays point at a row's id and what removing that row does to them.

exports.name: ReferenceSource
exports.description: One referencing array and the keys of its rows that hold a referenced id.

exports.name: ReferenceStore
exports.description:
The store surface the guard needs, untyped by path because a guard is
configured with plain strings. A `FormStore<T>` is assignable (method
parameters are bivariant), like `PluginStore`.

exports.name: NUMBER_EMPTY
exports.description: How an empty number input is stored. Canonical list for UIs and docs.

exports.name: parseNumberInput
exports.description:
Parse the raw text of a number input. Blank, partial (`"-"`, `"1e"`) or
non-finite input yields the empty value of `policy` (`undefined` by default,
or `null`); anything else is a finite number.
exports.signature: (raw: string, policy?: NumberEmpty) => number | null | undefined

exports.name: FORM_KEY_SEPARATOR
exports.description: Separator between path segments in a posted key (the canonical path spelling, `items.0.qty`).

exports.name: FORM_TRUE
exports.description: The text a `true` boolean posts (what a checked checkbox's hidden input carries).

exports.name: formEntries
exports.description:
The entries `value` posts under `name` (see the module comment for the rules).
`name` is a canonical dot path; `""` spreads an object's keys at the top level.

exports.name: toFormData
exports.description: Append every entry of `values` to `target` (a new `FormData` by default) and return it.

exports.name: FormEntry
exports.description: One posted pair. The value is text or a file blob, like a real `FormData` entry.

exports.name: FIELD_LEAF_KINDS
exports.description:
Kinds of the leaves INSIDE an object/array-valued widget that are not text
(`price.amount` is a number, `files.0.size` too); every other leaf is text.
Keyed by widget type, then by the leaf's last key.

exports.name: FIELD_VALUE_KINDS
exports.description: Value kind of every shipped widget type. A type missing here decodes as text.

exports.name: VALUE_KINDS
exports.description: Kinds of value a field node holds. Canonical list for registries and decoders.

exports.name: ValueKind
exports.description: A kind of value a field node holds (see {@link VALUE_KINDS}).

exports.name: FORM_STATE_STATUSES
exports.description:
Outcome of one server round trip:
- `idle` — nothing submitted yet, or an `$intent` (array add/remove) was applied without submitting
- `invalid` — server validation failed; `issues` lists the field messages
- `success` — the handler ran; `result` is what it returned
- `error` / `conflict` — the handler threw; `error` is the SubmitError JSON (its `fields` are also in `issues`)

exports.name: INTENT_ACTIONS
exports.description: Intents a button may carry. Canonical list.

exports.name: INTENT_KEY
exports.description: The posted key carrying an intent (reserved: never decoded as a value).

exports.name: INTENT_SEPARATOR
exports.description: Separates the action from its target in an intent value (`append:items`).

exports.name: initialFormState
exports.description:
The state before any submit: `useActionState(action, initialFormState())`.
`R` defaults to `never` so the initial state fits an action of any result type.

exports.name: intentValue
exports.description: The intent value a button posts.

exports.name: isFormState
exports.description: Structural check for a {@link FormState} (a value read back from an untyped boundary).

exports.name: parseIntent
exports.description: Parse an intent value; `undefined` when malformed or unknown (ignored, never thrown).

exports.name: FormState
exports.description: `R` is what the handler returns on success.

props.name: status
props.description: Outcome of the round trip.

props.name: values
props.description: The values as posted and decoded (files stripped) — a no-JS re-render keeps what the user typed.

props.name: issues
props.description: Field (and form-level, path `""`) messages, H10-shaped: the client's `setServerErrors` accepts them.

props.name: result
props.description: What the handler returned, on `success`.

props.name: error
props.description: The thrown SubmitError as JSON, on `error` or `conflict`.

exports.name: FormStateStatus
exports.description: Outcome of one server round trip (see {@link FORM_STATE_STATUSES} for what each means).

exports.name: Intent
exports.description: A parsed intent. `path` is the array (append) or the row (remove: `items.2`).

exports.name: IntentAction
exports.description: An array action a no-JS button can post: `append` or `remove` (see {@link INTENT_ACTIONS}).

exports.name: PostedValues
exports.description: Decoded posted values: untyped by nature (a post is not validated yet), narrowed by the definition only on success.

exports.name: NumberEmpty
exports.description: How an empty number input is stored: `undefined` or `null` (see {@link NUMBER_EMPTY}).

exports.name: DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER_MS
exports.description: Wait used for a 429 that names no `Retry-After` (ms). Long enough not to hammer a limiter, short enough to read.

exports.name: HTTP_STATUS
exports.description: The HTTP statuses the submit-recovery paths branch on.

exports.name: isSubmitError
exports.description: Structural check: a {@link SubmitError} instance or its plain JSON shape (field messages must be strings).

exports.name: parseRetryAfter
exports.description:
`Retry-After` in ms: delta-seconds or an HTTP date (measured from `now`).
`undefined` when absent or unreadable; never negative.
exports.signature: (header: string | null, now?: number) => number | undefined

exports.name: SUBMIT_ERROR_CODES
exports.description: Machine codes the store itself produces (an author's `code` is any string).

exports.name: SUBMIT_ERROR_DEFAULT_MESSAGE
exports.description: Default form-level text when a SubmitError carries only field messages.

exports.name: SUBMIT_ERROR_KIND
exports.description: Discriminator of the plain JSON shape; a value carrying it is a submit error.

exports.name: SubmitError
exports.description:
A submit failure with field messages. Throw it from `onSubmit` (or return its
JSON from a server action). `T` types `fields` keys against the form's paths.

exports.name: submitErrorFromResponse
exports.description:
Turn a non-2xx response into the {@link SubmitError} the store knows how to
recover from. Body convention, all optional:
`{ message?: string, fields?: { [path]: string }, current?: <the record> }`
(`current` is the server's version of the record on a 409/412). Use it in a
submit handler: `if (!res.ok) throw await submitErrorFromResponse(res)`.

- 403 → `forbidden` (the CSRF retry hook)
- 409 / 412 → `conflict: true`, `theirs` = `current`
- 422 → `validation` with `fields`
- 429 → `rate_limited`, retryable, `retryAfterMs` from `Retry-After` (default {@link DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER_MS})
- 5xx → `http`, retryable; anything else → `http`

exports.name: HttpResponseLike
exports.description: The part of a fetch `Response` the mapper reads (any HTTP client's response can be adapted to it).

exports.name: SubmitErrorInit
exports.description:
The agreed shape:
- `message` — form-level text, shown by `Form.Status`
- `fields` — field path → message; applied as server errors on those fields
- `code` — optional machine code (`"card_declined"`, or one of {@link SUBMIT_ERROR_CODES})
- `retryable` — `Form.Status` offers `retry()` when true
- `conflict` — a 409-style conflict: status becomes `"conflict"` instead of `"error"`
- `status` — the HTTP status when the failure came from a response (403 drives the CSRF retry)
- `retryAfterMs` — a rate limit's wait; the store refuses to resubmit until it passes
- `theirs` — on a conflict, the server's CURRENT record (any JSON value; the
  form's value shape when the server follows the convention) for the theirs-vs-mine view

exports.name: SubmitErrorJSON
exports.description: The plain JSON form of a {@link SubmitError} (what a server action returns).

exports.name: DEFAULT_ERROR_SOURCES
exports.description: What `mapErrors` tries when no `sources` are passed: the server's message, form-level.

exports.name: graphQLResponseOf
exports.description:
The GraphQL response envelope (`{ errors?, data? }`, per the GraphQL spec)
inside `input`: the response itself, or a client error that carries it on
`.response` (graphql-request's `ClientError` and similar wrappers).

exports.name: isErrorRecord
exports.description: True for a non-null, non-array object (a JSON record or a class instance).

exports.name: joinFieldSegments
exports.description:
`["lines", 0, "qty"]` → `lines.0.qty`. Leading segments listed in
`dropLeading` are removed first (a backend that prefixes every field with
its input argument passes that name); the last segment is never dropped.
Non-string, non-number segments are ignored; an empty result is `undefined`.
exports.signature: (segments: readonly unknown[], dropLeading?: readonly string[]) => string | undefined

exports.name: mapErrors
exports.description:
Turn a server failure into a {@link SubmitError}, or `undefined` when no
source recognised it or it carried no issues (a clean payload).
Field issues go to `fields` (first message per path wins); form-level and
unmapped issues join into `message`. `code` = the first issue's code, or
`validation` when every issue landed on a field.

In an `onSubmit`: `const err = mapErrors(res, { sources, paths }); if (err) throw err`.
exports.signature: <T = unknown>(input: unknown, opts?: MapErrorsOptions<T>) => SubmitError<T> | undefined

exports.name: messageSource
exports.description:
The backend-neutral default: ONE form-level issue carrying the server's own
words. Reads, in order, the first `errors[].message` of a GraphQL response
(the spec's shape — field locations are NOT read, that is a convention), then
a thrown Error's (or `{ message }` object's) `message`. Recognises nothing
else, so a clean payload maps to `undefined`.

exports.name: nonEmptyString
exports.description: `x` when it is a non-empty string, else `undefined`.

exports.name: ErrorPathMap
exports.description:
Server field name → form path. A record maps exact names (`"account_id": "setup.accountId"`);
a function decides per name. Return `null` (or omit the key) to keep the issue form-level.

exports.name: ErrorSource
exports.description:
Recognise one wire shape. Returns `undefined` when `input` is not that shape
(so the next source gets a chance), or the issues it found (possibly none).

exports.name: MapErrorsOptions
exports.description: Options of mapping a server error onto form paths: the wire shapes to recognise, the name-to-path map and the known paths.

exports.name: RawIssue
exports.description: One failure as the server named it. `field` is the server's field name (dot-joined); absent = form-level.

exports.name: commitSubForm
exports.description:
Write a finished sub-form into the parent: the slice at `scope` plus every
`also` write, as one user batch (one undo step, one change event).
exports.signature: <T extends object, P extends FieldPath<T>>(parent: FormStore<T>, scope: P, values: FieldValue<T, P>, also?: readonly SubFormWrite<T>[]) => void

exports.name: commitSubFormPick
exports.description:
Write a finished pick sub-form into the parent: every picked key the parent
holds, plus every `also` write, as ONE user batch (one undo step, one change
event listing each written path). A picked key the parent does not hold is
skipped, never created.
exports.signature: <T extends object, K extends FieldPath<T>>(parent: FormStore<T>, keys: readonly K[], values: SubFormPick<T, K>, also?: readonly SubFormWrite<T>[]) => void

exports.name: subFormSeed
exports.description:
The scratch store's starting values: the parent's value at `scope` now, or
`fallback` when the parent has none there yet (a first-time setup).
exports.signature: <T extends object, P extends FieldPath<T>>(parent: FormStore<T>, scope: P, fallback: SubFormValues<T, P>) => SubFormValues<T, P>

exports.name: subFormSeedFrom
exports.description:
{@link subFormSeed} for a slice addressed at runtime (a repeater row the
dialog was opened from, where the path carries a row index the types cannot
know): `current` when it is an object, else `fallback`.
exports.signature: <C extends object>(current: unknown, fallback: C) => C

exports.name: subFormSeedPick
exports.description:
The scratch store's starting values for a pick sub-form: each picked key's
current parent value, or its `fallback` value when the parent has none there.
exports.signature: <T extends object, K extends FieldPath<T>>(parent: FormStore<T>, keys: readonly K[], fallback: SubFormPick<T, K>) => SubFormPick<T, K>

exports.name: PipelinePhase

exports.name: SubmitPipeline

The scratch values of a pick sub-form: exactly the picked keys, each typed by

exports.name: SubFormWrite
