exports.name: createOptimisticList
exports.description: Create an optimistic list seeded with the items the page already shows.

exports.name: OptimisticContext
exports.description: The slice of a submit's context a change needs (the `ctx` a submit handler gets).

exports.name: OptimisticEntry
exports.description: One row as shown: the item and whether the server has yet to confirm it.

exports.name: OptimisticList
exports.description: A host-owned list that shows submitted changes at once and rolls each back if its submit fails.

exports.name: OptimisticListOptions
exports.description: Options of {@link createOptimisticList}.

exports.name: CONFLICT_KINDS
exports.description: How a differing path came to differ (see the file header).

exports.name: CONFLICT_PICKS
exports.description: Which side a true conflict keeps.

exports.name: diffConflict
exports.description: Every path where `mine` and `theirs` differ, classified against `base`. Pure.
exports.signature: (args: { base: unknown; mine: unknown; theirs: unknown; }) => ConflictField[]

exports.name: mergeConflict
exports.description:
The merged values: start from `theirs`, keep every `mine` row, and for each
`both` row take `picks[path]` (default {@link CONFLICT_PICKS.mine}).
exports.signature: <V>(theirs: V, rows: readonly ConflictField[], picks?: Readonly<Record<string, ConflictPick>>) => V

exports.name: resolveConflict
exports.description:
Accept the server's record as the new baseline (so the next submit carries
ITS lock token) and keep this tab's kept changes as unsaved edits on top:
`theirs` → baseline, merged values → current values (dirty where they differ).
Then the user reviews and submits again. Returns the rows it resolved.
exports.signature: <T extends object>(store: ConflictStore<T>, theirs: T, picks?: Readonly<Record<string, ConflictPick>>) => ConflictField[]

exports.name: ConflictField
exports.description: One path where mine and theirs disagree.

exports.name: ConflictKind
exports.description: How a differing path came to differ: changed by `mine`, by `theirs`, or by `both` (see {@link CONFLICT_KINDS}).

exports.name: ConflictPick
exports.description: The side a true conflict keeps: `mine` or `theirs` (see {@link CONFLICT_PICKS}).

exports.name: ConflictStore
exports.description: The store surface {@link resolveConflict} needs (a `FormStore` is one).

exports.name: ArrayApi
exports.description:
Structural operations on one array path (K3). Every mutation is
one undo step, one flush and one change event, and moves field state
(errors, touched, registrations) with its row. `Row` is the element type
(`FieldValue<T, P>[number]` through `FormStore.array`); untyped callers get
`unknown`.

exports.name: ArrayElement
exports.description: Element type of an array value (`unknown` when the value is not an array).

exports.name: ArrayRow
exports.description: One row as {@link ArrayApi.rows} reports it: stable id, current index, current value.

exports.name: CompositeSnapshot
exports.description: N11 — what `store.getComposite(key)` reports: the control value and the composite's rule state.

exports.name: CreateFormStoreConfig
exports.description: Configuration of {@link createFormStore}: default values, model, schema, validation timing and plugins.

exports.name: CsrfOptions
exports.description: See {@link CreateFormStoreConfig.csrf}.

exports.name: ExitHold
exports.description: A standing exit hold (see {@link FormStore.holdExit}).

exports.name: FormInspection
exports.description: A point-in-time view of the store for tooling ({@link FormStore.inspect}).

exports.name: IssueSource
exports.description: Where an issue came from: `schema`, `rule`, `required` or `server` (see {@link ISSUE_SOURCES}).

exports.name: IssueTrace
exports.description: One current issue with its origin: `rule` names the model rule ("minLength", "count", a registry validator) when known.

exports.name: SchemaReports
exports.description: How completely a schema reports issues: `auto`, `all` or `first` (see {@link SCHEMA_REPORTS}).

exports.name: FormStore
exports.description:
The form kernel. `T` is the value shape, `TOut` the payload (after
`toSubmit`), `TResult` what the submit handler returns (`getResult()`).
exports.typeParameters: <T extends object, TOut = T, TResult = unknown>

exports.name: RemoveDecision
exports.description:
A guard's answer: block with a reason, or allow — optionally running
`before` (a cascade or nullify) in the SAME batch as the removal, so one
undo restores both.

exports.name: RemoveGuard
exports.description: Decides whether a row of one array may be removed (referential integrity, "last admin" rules…).

exports.name: RemoveOutcome
exports.description: What {@link ArrayApi.remove} did: removed, or refused with a reason a UI can show.

exports.name: RemoveRequest
exports.description: The row a remove guard is asked about.

exports.name: NodeHandle
exports.description: A live JSX node registration (see {@link FormStore.registerNode}).

exports.name: Registration
exports.description:
A live field registration returned by {@link FormStore.register}.

Why it exists: a field inside a FieldArray row is addressed by its index path
(`items.2.qty`), but its identity is the row. The store moves the handle with
its row on every array op and undo/redo, so `path` is always where the
registration lives NOW. `release()` unregisters that current path, never the
path it was created with — React runs every unregister cleanup before the
re-registers on a reorder, and releasing by the old name would wipe a
conditional field of whichever row moved into that slot.

Invariant: `path` is `null` once released or once its row was removed;
`release()` is then a no-op, so it is always safe to call.

exports.name: RestoredOutcome
exports.description: A submit outcome to rehydrate with {@link FormStore.restoreSubmit}.

exports.name: RowId
exports.description:
Stable identity of one array row. Minted by the store, never
reused, kept across move/insert/remove and undo/redo; a plain string at
runtime (React keys, DOM ids), branded so an index cannot be passed where an
id is meant.

exports.name: RowTarget
exports.description: A row addressed by its current index or by its stable id (an unknown id is a no-op).

exports.name: ScopeStatus
exports.description: See {@link FormStore.scopeStatus}. `total` = active fields considered; `filled`/`requiredFilled` count non-empty ones.

exports.name: IsDirtyOpts
exports.description: Options of {@link FormStore.isDirty} (gap L).

exports.name: SetOpts
exports.description: Options of a store write such as `setValue`.

exports.name: SubmitContext
exports.description: What a submit handler receives besides the payload.

exports.name: SubmitOpts
exports.description: Options of {@link FormStore.submit}.

exports.name: InferInput
exports.description: The input type of a Standard Schema.

exports.name: InferOutput
exports.description: The output type of a Standard Schema.

exports.name: StandardIssue
exports.description: One validation issue: its message and the path it is on.

exports.name: StandardSchemaV1
exports.description: A validator that implements Standard Schema v1 (Zod, Valibot, ArkType…), the only validation contract the core speaks.

exports.name: createTranslator
exports.description: Build a translator over a bundle, with optional single-key overrides on top. Plural rules are built once per translator, on first use.

exports.name: DE_MESSAGES
exports.description: The German catalog — the second locale, proof that every key is translatable.

exports.name: EN_MESSAGES
exports.description:
The English catalog — the source of every key. Grouped by the layer that
renders the text; the key prefix names that layer (`rule.*`, `array.*` are
core issues; `fieldArray.*`, `wizard.*` the React primitives; the rest the
styled fields). Keep keys stable: they are a public API for translators.

exports.name: EN_TRANSLATOR
exports.description: The English translator every store and component falls back to.

exports.name: FORM_MESSAGES
exports.description: The form catalog as the shared

exports.name: formatMessage
exports.description: Render one template: pick the plural form by `params.n`, then fill the placeholders.
exports.signature: (template: MessageTemplate, params?: MessageParams, locale?: string) => string

exports.name: interpolate
exports.description: Fill `{name}` placeholders. Unknown names stay as written, so a typo is visible instead of silently blank.

exports.name: MESSAGE_BUNDLES
exports.description: The bundles that ship with the engine, keyed by locale; the canonical list of built-in locales.

exports.name: PLURAL_CATEGORIES
exports.description: CLDR plural categories (`Intl.PluralRules#select` results).

exports.name: PLURAL_PARAM
exports.description: The param that selects a plural form.

exports.name: pluralCategory
exports.description: The plural category of `n` in `locale`; `other` for an unknown locale.

exports.name: regionName
exports.description: A region's display name ("DE" → "Germany" / "Deutschland") from `Intl.DisplayNames`; the code itself when the platform has no names.

exports.name: weekdayName
exports.description:
The name of weekday `index` (0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday, ISO order) in `locale`,
from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` — day names are locale data, not catalog keys, so
every locale the platform knows works without a translation.

exports.name: BuiltinLocale
exports.description: A locale with a message bundle shipped in {@link MESSAGE_BUNDLES} (`en`, `de`).

exports.name: MessageBundle
exports.description: A locale tag plus its catalog.

exports.name: MessageCatalog
exports.description: A complete locale: every key defined.

exports.name: MessageKey
exports.description: Every message key (the canonical list is `Object.keys(EN_MESSAGES)`).

exports.name: MessageParams
exports.description: Values substituted into `{name}` placeholders. `n` also selects the plural form.

exports.name: MessageTemplate
exports.description: One catalog entry: a plain template or plural forms. `{name}` is replaced by the `name` param.

exports.name: PluralCategory
exports.description: One CLDR plural category: `zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many` or `other`.

exports.name: PluralForms
exports.description: A plural message: one template per category the locale uses; `other` is required, it is the fallback.

exports.name: Translator
exports.description:
Resolves keys to text for one locale. `t` never throws and never returns a
key name: every catalog is complete by type.

exports.name: AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS
exports.description: Default debounce for `on: "change"` (ms).

exports.name: AUTOSAVE_FAILED_MESSAGE
exports.description: Message when a save rejects with something that is not an Error.

exports.name: AUTOSAVE_TRIGGERS
exports.description: When a field is saved.

exports.name: SAVE_STATUSES
exports.description: Save status of one field, held in its `FieldRecord.save` (absent = never saved).

exports.name: AutosaveContext
exports.description: What `save` receives besides the patch. `V` is the form's value type.

exports.name: AutosaveOptions
exports.description: The store's `autosave` option: the per-field save call, its trigger and debounce, and which paths it covers.

exports.name: AutosaveTrigger
exports.description: When autosave writes a field: on `blur`, or on a debounced `change` (see {@link AUTOSAVE_TRIGGERS}).

props.name: status
props.description: Where the field's last save stands.

props.name: error
props.description: The failure message when `status` is `"error"`.

exports.name: SaveStatus
exports.description: One field's save status: `saving`, `saved` or `error` (see {@link SAVE_STATUSES}).

exports.name: createHistorySearchAdapter
exports.description: The current page's query string via `history.replaceState` + `popstate`. Safe on the server (empty, no writes).

exports.name: decodeParam
exports.description: Decode one key from the params, typed by its default; `undefined` when absent or malformed.
exports.signature: (params: URLSearchParams, key: string, fallback: unknown) => unknown

exports.name: encodeParams
exports.description: Write the mirrored keys into a copy of `base` (other params kept): defaults omitted, arrays repeated.
exports.signature: (base: URLSearchParams, values: Values, defaults: Values, keys: readonly string[]) => URLSearchParams

exports.name: live
exports.description: Emit the payload after changes settle — the "no submit button" mode of a filter or search form.

exports.name: LIVE_DEBOUNCE_MS
exports.description: Default debounce of both plugins (ms).

exports.name: urlState
exports.description: Mirror filter values to the query string and back.

exports.name: LiveOptions
exports.description: Options of the `live` plugin: what to call with the payload and how long changes must settle.

exports.name: SearchParamsAdapter
exports.description:
Where the query string lives. The app supplies one for its router (a
TanStack Router adapter belongs in app code, like the wizard's step
adapter); {@link createHistorySearchAdapter} uses the History API directly.

exports.name: UrlStateOptions
exports.description: Options of the `urlState` plugin: the search-params adapter, the keys to mirror and the debounce.

exports.name: CASE_SEPARATOR
exports.description: Separator for a builder case key matching several values (`"sql|sql_batch"`).

exports.name: DEFAULT_CASE
exports.description: Case key for the fallback branch of a builder variant.

exports.name: FIELD_TYPES
exports.description: Field-type helpers shipped by name. Every one is `field(type, name, opts)`; third-party types use `field` directly.

exports.name: clean
exports.description: Drop `undefined` members so equal definitions are deep-equal whichever front-end built them.

exports.name: defineForm
exports.description:
Define a form against its value type: `defineForm<Checkout>()(({ f, c, e, v }) => ({ fields: […] }))`.
Curried so `T` is given explicitly while the callback stays inferred.
`D` declares computed keys OUTSIDE `T`: `defineForm<Invoice, { total: number }>()`
lets `derived: { total: … }` and refs to `total` type-check, keeps `total` out of
`FieldPath<Invoice>` (so `setValue("total")` does not compile), and types
`readComputed(form, def, "total")` as `number`.

Invariant: the result is plain data (plus marked escapes). A definition with
`strict: true` throws here if it contains any escape hatch.
exports.signature: <T, D extends object = NoComputed>() => (build: (kits: Kits<T & D>) => DefInput<T & D>) => FormDef<T, D>

exports.name: isBuiltExpr
exports.description: Was `v` produced by a builder (so it is an expression, not a literal)?

exports.name: kit
exports.description: The typed kits for `T` at the form root (absolute names and refs). Also handy for JSX props: `const { c, v } = kit<Checkout>()`.

exports.name: readComputed
exports.description:
Read a computed key declared outside `T` (`defineForm<T, D>()`), typed by
the definition. Read-only by construction: `D`'s paths are not `FieldPath<T>`,
so no typed setter accepts them, and the store throws on a computed path.
exports.typeParameters: <T, D extends object, P extends FieldPath<D>>
exports.signature: <T, D extends object, P extends FieldPath<D>>(store: { getValues(): unknown; }, _def: FormDef<T, D>, path: P) => FieldValue<D, P> | undefined

exports.name: toDeriveSpec
exports.description: `derive` input → canonical {@link DeriveSpec}.

exports.name: Arg
exports.description: A literal or a builder expression, in a value position.

exports.name: ArrayOpts
exports.description: Options for array nodes. `layout`/`addMenu`/`virtualize` are presentation, copied into `props`.

exports.name: ArrayPath
exports.description: Paths of `T` whose value is an array.

exports.name: ArrayRef
exports.description: An array ref: a typed array path of `T` or a relative/root ref.

exports.name: ArraySource
exports.description:
N11 — what `e.map` / `e.filter` iterate: an array ref, or any array EXPRESSION
(`e.lookup("channels")`, another `e.map`), so an option table can be filtered
by the sibling rows' values.

exports.name: Children
exports.description: Children of a group: one node, a list, or a callback given the group's relative kit.

exports.name: CondKit
exports.description: Condition builders typed against scope `T`. The left side is a path of `T` (value typed), a relative ref or an expression.

exports.name: CountOpts
exports.description: Message overrides and the row target of a `count` rule (see {@link CountRule }).

exports.name: DefInput
exports.description: What a `defineForm` callback returns. Derived keys, effect targets and action targets are paths of `T`.

exports.name: CompositeOpts
exports.description: Options of a model composite (`f.composite(id, opts)`); see `CompositeNode`.

exports.name: CompositeWriteOpt
exports.description: One write-back step of `f.composite`: `to` (an expression; `e.arg("value")` is the new control value) stored at `set`.

exports.name: DisplayOpts
exports.description: Options for display nodes (`format`/`live` copied into `props`).

exports.name: ElemFor
exports.description: Element scope for an array source: the typed element, or {@link Loose} for a relative ref or an expression.

exports.name: ElemKit
exports.description: Element-scope expression kit handed to `e.sum`/`e.map`/`c.all`… callbacks.

exports.name: ElementOf
exports.description: Element type of the array at path `P` of `T`.

exports.name: ExprKit
exports.description: Value-expression builders typed against scope `T`.

exports.name: FieldOpts
exports.description: Options every field builder accepts. Unlisted widget extras go in `props`.

exports.name: FieldTypeName
exports.description: A field type with a builder helper shipped by name (see {@link FIELD_TYPES}).

exports.name: GroupOpts
exports.description: Options for group nodes.

exports.name: GroupScope
exports.description: Scope type inside group `P` of `S`.

exports.name: Kits
exports.description: The four kits for a scope.

exports.name: Loose
exports.description: A loosely-typed scope (templates, relative arrays): any path, unknown values.

exports.name: MemberArg
exports.description: Candidate list for `in`/`notIn` with left side `L`.

exports.name: NodeKit
exports.description: Node builders typed against scope `S`.

exports.name: Ref
exports.description: A path a builder accepts: typed against the scope type, or an explicit relative/root ref.

exports.name: RefValue
exports.description: Value type a ref names: typed for a path of `T`, unknown for a relative/root ref.

exports.name: RelPath
exports.description: A scope-relative (`.qty`, `..rate`) or root-absolute (`/total`) ref; checked at runtime, not statically.

exports.name: RightArg
exports.description: Right-hand side of a comparison whose left side is `L`: typed by the field when `L` is a path of `T`.

exports.name: RowKit
exports.description: Kit for an array row or group scope: relative names, relative refs.

exports.name: TypedExpr
exports.description: A builder-made expression whose value type is `V` (phantom; no runtime cost).

exports.name: ValidatorKit
exports.description: Validator builders typed against scope `T`.

exports.name: VariantOpts
exports.description: Options of `f.variant` (H5 / D9).

exports.name: compile
exports.description:
Compile a definition. `extraDerived` are imperative registrations that join
the same graph. Throws {@link FormModelError} on any structural error.

exports.name: overlaps
exports.description:
Do two paths/patterns overlap — equal, or one an ancestor of the other —
with `*` matching any single segment? This is THE dependency rule: a change
at `items.3.qty` affects anything depending on `items` (ancestor),
`items.*.qty` (match) or `items.3` (descendant change).

exports.name: WILDCARD
exports.description: Wildcard segment matching one row index in a pattern.

exports.name: CompiledDerived
exports.description: One derived value at pattern level, in evaluation order.

exports.name: CompiledEffect
exports.description: One effect after compiling, with its triggers and write targets resolved to absolute patterns.

exports.name: CompiledModel
exports.description: A form definition compiled for the runtime: derived values in evaluation order, effects and the dependency sets.

exports.name: CONTEXT_DEP_PREFIX
exports.description:
Dependency prefix of an app-context read: `{ ctx: "plan" }` depends on
`$ctx.plan`. `$` cannot start a form field name, so it never collides with
a value path; the store flushes `$ctx.<key>` when that key changes.

exports.name: CORE_OPERATORS
exports.description: Core operator names (closed set) plus the form extensions. Registered operators may not shadow them.

exports.name: collectDeps
exports.description:
Static dependency extraction: every path an expression may read, as written
(relative refs stay relative; `/x` becomes `x`).

Inside the element expression of map/sum/count/… over a form path `P`, an
element ref `qty` is recorded as `P.*.qty` (a whole-element ref as `P.*`),
so editing an unrelated column of a 1,000-row table does not recompute a sum
over another column. A change that replaces or resizes `P` still overlaps
those patterns (it is their ancestor). Over a computed array (no path) the
element refs add nothing: that array's own deps already cover them.

`element` = the wildcard base of the innermost element scope (`null` when
not inside one, `""` inside one whose array has no form path).
exports.signature: (expr: Expr, element?: string | null, out?: string[]) => string[]

exports.name: collectOperators
exports.description: Every operator name used in `expr` that is not a core operator (for loud `fromJSON` checks).

exports.name: contextKeyOf
exports.description:
The app-context key a dependency string names (`"$ctx.propertyId"` → `"propertyId"`),
or `undefined` for a form path. Effects (`on`) and resource deps use it to tell an
app-context trigger from a value path (gap C).

exports.name: evaluate
exports.description: Evaluate an expression. Throws {@link FormModelError} on an unknown operator (never a silent false).

exports.name: isEmptyValue
exports.description: Empty for the `empty`/`filled` operators: null, undefined, "", [] or NaN (NOT false).

exports.name: resolveRef
exports.description:
Turn a scope-relative or root-absolute ref into a canonical absolute path.
`.x` → innermost scope + x; each extra leading dot climbs one scope; `/x` →
x. Plain names are returned unchanged (callers decide absolute vs element).

exports.name: truthy
exports.description: JSON Logic truthiness: an empty array is falsy, everything else as JS.

exports.name: EvalContext
exports.description: Everything an expression may read. Built by the runtime per evaluation site.

exports.name: allNodeLists
exports.description: Every node list in a definition (fields + templates), for walkers that must see all of them.

exports.name: fromJSON
exports.description:
Validate untrusted JSON and return it as a {@link FormDef}. Throws
{@link FormModelError} naming the first problem found.

exports.name: toJSON
exports.description:
Serialize a definition. Undefined members are dropped, so two definitions
that differ only by absent-vs-undefined keys serialize identically.
Throws {@link FormModelError} `not serializable` when `strict` and any escape exists.

exports.name: assembleNodes
exports.description:
Build the node tree from live registrations. Children follow registration
order; identical siblings (the same template rendered for several rows)
collapse into one. A `use` registration contributes a `use` node in place
and its children become the template body; the first instance that rendered
any children defines it (a recursion-stopped instance renders none).

exports.name: fieldNodeFrom
exports.description: Build the node a JSX field registers. Undefined props are omitted, so it deep-equals the builder's node.

exports.name: relativize
exports.description:
Rewrite concrete scoped paths into relative ones. For scopes `[outer, …, inner]`
a string inside `inner` (`inner.<n>.rest` for a row scope, `inner.rest` for a
named scope) becomes `.rest`, inside `outer` `..rest` (one more dot per level
out). Strings already relative are left alone.

exports.name: AssembledModel
exports.description: What assembly produces: the root nodes plus the template bodies learned from `<FieldTemplate>` instances.

exports.name: CaseEntry
exports.description: A case of a JSX `<Variant>`: `is` values, or the fallback when `isDefault`.

exports.name: FieldSpec
exports.description:
The model-relevant props of a JSX field. `required` keeps the original meaning of
a string (the message); an expression object makes it `requiredIf`.

exports.name: ModelScope
exports.description:
One enclosing JSX scope, as assembly sees it. Two shapes:
- `{ path: "items", row: true }` — a `<FieldArray>`; any `items.<n>` prefix is that array's row scope
  (render-prop rows build their names by index, so the row number is matched, not known)
- `{ path: "billing", row: false }` — a `<FieldScope>` / scoped `<Wizard.Step>`; the exact prefix

exports.name: NodeEntry
exports.description: What one mounted JSX component contributes: a node WITHOUT its children, or a variant case.

exports.name: NodeRegistration
exports.description: One live JSX registration.

exports.name: FromJSONOptions
exports.description: What `fromJSON` checks names against. Omit `loaders`/`widgetTypes` to skip those checks (e.g. a server without UI).

exports.name: NonSerializableEntry
exports.description: One escape hatch found by {@link toJSON}: where it is and which paths it reads.

exports.name: ToJSONResult
exports.description: What {@link toJSON} returns: the JSON definition and every escape hatch it could not serialize.

exports.name: createRegistry
exports.description: An empty registry. Every store without an explicit `registry` uses a fresh one.

exports.name: CodecDef
exports.description: A named display ⇄ canonical codec (the field catalog ships them; the model only resolves names).

exports.name: EffectDef
exports.description: A named effect step (`{ op, args }`). Writes go through `set`, the same pipeline as declarative steps.

exports.name: ModelRegistry
exports.description:
The registry. Read with `get*`/`has*`; extend with the builder methods, each
returning a new registry that also holds every earlier registration.

exports.name: OperatorDef
exports.description: A named expression operator. `fn` receives the evaluated arguments.

exports.name: ValidatorContext
exports.description: Context handed to a named validator.

exports.name: ValidatorDef
exports.description: A named validator: returns a message when invalid, `undefined` when valid.

exports.name: arrayLimitMessage
exports.description:
The display text for an array's `bound` limit: the node's own message or the
catalog default (`array.min` is phrased as a reason, "required", because it
also explains a disabled Remove), with `{n}` filled. Shared by validation and
every gated control so the reason a button is disabled always matches the
issue a submit reports — pass the form's translator so both speak its locale.
exports.signature: (node: Pick<ArrayNode, "min" | "max" | "minMessage" | "maxMessage">, bound: ArrayBound, messages?: Translator) => string

exports.name: MAX_EFFECT_DEPTH
exports.description: Effects triggered by effect writes stop after this many levels.

exports.name: STALE_OPTION_MESSAGE
exports.description: English message for a value no longer among its field's options (prefill keeps it, validation flags it); the catalog key is `staleOption`.

exports.name: textOf
exports.description: Resolve a {@link Text} to a display string (i18n resolution is the renderer's job; this is the default).

exports.name: ArrayBound
exports.description: Which row-count limit of an array a message is about.

exports.name: CompositeInstance
exports.description: N11 — one composite in the walk: its node, where it evaluates, and its rule state (`required` is always false: a composite has no value of its own).

exports.name: ModelLoader
exports.description: A named async loader: gets the dependency VALUES in `deps` order.

exports.name: RuleState
exports.description: Model-derived state of one path, mirrored onto its `FieldRecord`.

props.name: active
props.description: Whether the path is active (visible and sent); `false` when a rule hides it.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the model makes the path required.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether a `disabledIf` rule disables the path.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether a `readOnlyIf` rule makes the path read-only.

props.name: options
props.description: The field's current options, when the model supplies them.

props.name: inherited
props.description: Gap H — the first non-empty link of the field's `inherit` chain (absent without a chain or when every link is empty).

exports.name: COMPOSITE_CONTROLS_BOOLEAN
exports.description: Composite control types whose value is a boolean (a native post reads `"true"` / `"on"` as true).

exports.name: COMPOSITE_KEY_MARK
exports.description: Marks the composite segment of a key.

exports.name: compositeKey
exports.description: The instance key of composite `id` in the innermost scope of `scopes` (or the root).

exports.name: isCompositeKey
exports.description: Is `key` a composite key (its last segment starts with the mark)?

exports.name: BUILTIN_RULES
exports.description: Built-in rule names, defined once so the runtime switch and the JSON loader agree.

exports.name: COMPOSITE_VALUE_ARG
exports.description:
The argument a composite's `write` steps read the new control value from:
`{ arg: "value" }` (the same `arg` operator a named action reads its args with).

exports.name: FORM_DEF_VERSION
exports.description: Current `FormDefJSON` version. Bumped only on a breaking shape change.

exports.name: FormModelError
exports.description:
Every model failure. Thrown at definition/compile time for structural errors
(cycles, unknown names), reported through the event bus + console for runtime
ones (effect loop). `chain` names the paths involved, in order.

exports.name: isRule
exports.description: Narrow a validator to the built-in rule(s) named, so the runtime reads `value`/`ref`/`by` without casts.
exports.signature: <R extends BuiltinRule>(v: Validator, ...names: R[]) => v is RuleOf<R>

exports.name: NODE_KINDS
exports.description: Every model node kind (the `kind` discriminant of {@link Node}); the canonical list for exhaustive switches and JSON validation.

exports.name: ON_STALE
exports.description: What happens to a value that is no longer among its field's options.

exports.name: ROW_ACTIONS
exports.description: Per-row controls a repeater renders; the canonical list is {@link ROW_ACTIONS}.

exports.name: WHEN_DISABLED
exports.description:
N6 — what a DISABLED field (`disabledIf`) does to the payload. Closed set:
- `omit` — left out of the payload, and not validated (HTML semantics; the default)
- `send` — still sent with its current value (an app whose backend expects the key, e.g. a "Not sure" row's empty ID); still not validated

exports.name: WHEN_HIDDEN
exports.description: What happens to a field's stored value when it becomes inactive. Default `clear`.

exports.name: ArrayNode
exports.description:
A list; `children` is the row template, relative to each row. `min`/`max`
compile to minItems/maxItems. The repeater chrome is part of the
node so AutoForm renders the same repeater JSX does: `rowActions`, `addLabel`
(the Add button text), `emptyText` (shown with no rows), `rowTitle` (an
expression evaluated in the row scope, the title of a `"cards"` row).
`props.layout` is `"stack"` (default) | `"table"` | `"cards"`.

exports.name: CompositeNode
exports.description:
N11 — ONE control over SEVERAL stored paths ("track this event" is one switch
but two stored booleans). Pathless: it owns no value of its own, so it has no
record, issues or payload entry; the paths it writes are ordinary values
(with their own nodes, rules and `whenHidden`, or none).

- `read` — the control value, an expression in the node's scope (`.a`, `/x`, `e.*`);
  it may not read `arg`.
- `write` — the steps that store a new control value, run in order (each sees the
  writes before it) as ONE user batch: one undo step, one change event. `to`
  reads the new value as `{ arg: "value" }` ({@link COMPOSITE_VALUE_ARG}).
- `id` — names the composite in its scope; its instance key is
  `compositeKey(scope, id)` (`@track`, `events.2.@track`), what the store API,
  the React hook and a native post use. Unique per scope.
- `type` — the control (`"switch"`, `"checkbox"`, `"select"`… a registry widget type).
- `visibleIf` / `disabledIf` / `readOnlyIf` gate the control like any node;
  `whenHidden` does not apply (there is no own value to clear).

Not on a composite (no path to put an issue on): `required`, `rules`, `warn` —
validate the stored paths instead, or with a form-level `assert`.

exports.name: CompositeWriteStep
exports.description: One write-back step of a composite: the value of `to` (which may read `{ arg: "value" }`) at the path `set` (relative names allowed).

exports.name: Cond
exports.description: An expression used as a condition (truthiness decides). Same shape as {@link Expr}; the alias documents intent.

exports.name: ContainerNode
exports.description: The node kinds that hold children (and so open a path scope or a section).

exports.name: CountRule
exports.description:
Cross-row cardinality on an array (audit L1): the number of rows for which
`where` holds must be within `min`..`max` ("exactly one cover photo", "at most
two primary contacts"). `where` is evaluated in each ROW's scope, so `.cover`
reads that row's `cover`. Serializable — the same rule runs on a server.

Errors, both from one run:
- array level (at the array path): `message`, else `rule.count.exactly` /
  `atLeast` / `atMost` from the catalog, `{n}` = the bound that failed;
- row level, only when TOO MANY rows match: every matching row gets
  `rowMessage` (else `rule.count.row`) at `rowPath` — a relative path in the
  row (`.cover`). When `rowPath` is absent and `where` is a bare relative
  `var` (`{var: ".cover"}`), that field is the target; otherwise the row itself.
  A row's own field issue wins over this one.

exports.name: DeriveSpec
exports.description:
A computed value. `when` makes it a conditional mirror: computed
while `when` holds (and read-only when `readOnly`), editable otherwise.
`send` (default true) keeps it in the payload.

exports.name: DisplayNode
exports.description: Read-only rendering of a value (usually a derived one).

exports.name: Effect
exports.description: A model effect: when a trigger path changes (and `when` holds), run its steps.

exports.name: EffectContext
exports.description: What a `fn` effect step may do: read values and write through the same pipeline.

exports.name: EffectOrigin
exports.description:
Change origins an effect may react to. `context` (gap C) is a change of an
app-context key named in `on` with the dependency prefix (`"$ctx.accountId"`),
from `store.setContext`; it is opt-in, so an existing effect never fires on it.

exports.name: EffectStep
exports.description:
One step of an effect or action. Shapes:
`{set, to}` write an expression · `{reset}` back to the node default/baseline ·
`{clear}` to undefined · `{validate}` a path or `"form"` · `{load}` reload a
resource field · `{op, args}` a registered named effect · `{fn, deps}` escape.
Targets may be relative (`.unitPrice`) and may use `*` wildcards (`rows.*.hours`).

exports.name: Expr
exports.description:
A JSON-Logic-compatible expression. A JSON object with exactly one key is an
operation (`{"==":[{"var":"a"},1]}`); every other value is a literal. Array
arguments are evaluated element-wise (JSON Logic semantics); an object or an
array that must stay literal is wrapped in `{"lit": value}`.

Shapes: a JSON primitive (literal) · an array of expressions · `{op: args}`
(core, form-extension or registered operator) · `{"$fn": FnEscape}` (escape).

exports.name: FieldNode
exports.description: One value at a path, rendered by the registry widget named by `type`.

exports.name: FnEscape
exports.description:
The non-serializable escape. `call` gets the whole
value tree; `deps` is REQUIRED because the dependency graph needs edges —
the runtime only re-evaluates when one of these paths changes.

exports.name: FormDef
exports.description:
A form definition for values `T`. `D` types the DERIVED keys that live
outside `T` — a `total` the user never types, so it is not in the value type
and not settable — read with `readComputed` / `useComputed`.

exports.name: FormDefJSON
exports.description:
The serializable form of a definition: the same shape as {@link FormDef}, but
produced by `toJSON()`, so every escape hatch has been replaced by a marker
(`{"$fn":{"deps":[…]}}`, `{"rule":"fn","deps":[…]}`, `{"fn":{"deps":[…]}}`)
and the whole value survives `JSON.stringify` → `JSON.parse` unchanged.

exports.name: FormModelErrorKind
exports.description: Machine-readable kind of a {@link FormModelError}.

exports.name: GroupNode
exports.description: A path prefix (sub-object); children are relative to it. May mirror another value via `derive`.

exports.name: Json
exports.description: Any JSON value; form definitions hold only these so they serialize.

exports.name: JsonObject
exports.description: A JSON object of {@link Json} values.

exports.name: JsonPrimitive
exports.description: A JSON scalar: string, number, boolean or `null`.

exports.name: NamedValidator
exports.description: A registered validator referenced by name (serializable). `async.debounceMs` delays automatic runs.

exports.name: Node
exports.description: Every node kind a model tree holds; `kind` discriminates.

exports.name: NodeKind
exports.description: A model node kind, the `kind` discriminant of {@link Node} (see {@link NODE_KINDS}).

exports.name: OnStale
exports.description: What a value no longer among its options becomes: `clear`, `keep` or the `first` option (see {@link ON_STALE}).

exports.name: OptionItem
exports.description: One choice of an options field: the stored value, its label and whether it can be picked.

exports.name: OptionsSource
exports.description:
Where a field's options come from. Shapes: a static list · an expression
evaluated in the field's scope (e.g. `lookup("operators", …)`) · a resource
reference (object with a `resource` key).

exports.name: ResourceRef
exports.description: A named async loader reference. Loaders are code, supplied to the store by name.

exports.name: RuleOf
exports.description: A built-in rule narrowed by name (a named validator's `rule` is any other string, so `switch` cannot narrow).

exports.name: RowAction
exports.description: A per-row control of a repeater (see {@link ROW_ACTIONS}).

exports.name: RuleProps
exports.description: State rules every node kind may carry. Each condition is evaluated in the node's scope.

props.name: visibleIf
props.description: Condition under which the node shows; hidden nodes are inactive.

props.name: disabledIf
props.description: Condition under which the node is disabled.

props.name: readOnlyIf
props.description: Condition under which the node is read-only.

props.name: whenHidden
props.description: On a container (variant, scope, group, step) it is inherited by every field below; when a field hides, the policy of the container whose condition hid it applies (a field's own always wins).

exports.name: ScopeNode
exports.description: No path: carries rules for its children (what `<When>` compiles to).

exports.name: SectionNode
exports.description: Layout only: a titled block with a column count.

exports.name: StepNode
exports.description:
A wizard step. `scope` is a path prefix: children are relative to
it (like a group, without being a value node) and it is the subset validated
on Next. `visibleIf` makes the step conditional: an inactive step is skipped
and its fields neither validate nor submit.

exports.name: Text
exports.description: Serializable text: a plain string, or an i18n key with an optional default.

exports.name: UseNode
exports.description: Expands a named template in the current scope (recursion).

exports.name: Validator
exports.description:
One validation rule. Shapes by `rule`:
- `minLength`/`maxLength`/`min`/`max` — `value` is a number or an expression
- `pattern` — `value` is a RegExp source, `flags` optional
- `email` / `url` / `integer` — no argument
- `oneOf` — `value` is a literal list or an expression yielding one
- `matches` — `ref` is another field's path (confirm password)
- `unique` — on an array: rows unique by the relative key `by` (whole row when absent); the array gets
  `message`, and each row whose key repeats another gets `rowMessage` at `by` (the row when `by` is absent)
- `minItems` / `maxItems` — on an array
- `count` — on an array: how many rows satisfy `where` (cross-row cardinality, L1); see {@link CountRule}
- `assert` — `test` must be truthy; `path` targets another field (cross-field)
- `fn` — the non-serializable escape; `deps` required
- any other string — a validator registered by name in the {@link ModelRegistry }

exports.name: ValidatorFn
exports.description: Escape-hatch validator: returns a message (invalid) or undefined (valid), possibly async.

exports.name: VariantCase
exports.description: One case of a variant: active while the discriminant equals any of `is`.

exports.name: BranchDefaults
exports.description:
Per-branch defaults (H5): field name → value, seeded when the branch turns
active and the field's value is undefined (so a required field in a freshly
chosen branch starts valid instead of showing a phantom error). Names resolve
like field names in the variant's scope (`.x` is row-relative). A field's own
`default` wins over a branch default.

exports.name: NoComputed
exports.description: No computed keys outside `T` (the default `D` of {@link FormDef}).

exports.name: VariantNode
exports.description:
Switches child sets on a discriminant expression. Several cases may be active
at once (concatenated). Variants nest: a case may hold another variant, and a
switch of the outer discriminant deactivates the whole inner subtree in the
same flush (one walk to an activity fixpoint, then the clears and seeds).

Value retention on switch (D9): `whenHidden` on the variant is inherited by
every field below it (a field's own `whenHidden` wins) — `"clear"` (default)
drops the leaving branch's values, `"keep"` keeps them for switching back
(not submitted), `"keep-and-send"` keeps and submits them.

exports.name: WhenDisabled
exports.description: What a disabled field's value does: `omit` from the payload or `send` it (see {@link WHEN_DISABLED}).

exports.name: WhenHidden
exports.description: What an inactive field's value does: `clear`, `keep`, or `keep-and-send` (see {@link WHEN_HIDDEN}).

exports.name: CARD_BRANDS
exports.description: Brands the number field recognises. `unknown` groups as 4-4-4-4.

exports.name: CARD_CVC_MASK
exports.description: The security code's input mask: three digits and an optional fourth (Amex).

exports.name: CARD_EXPIRY_MASK
exports.description: The expiry's input mask (`MM/YY`); the field writes it eagerly, so `7` shows `07/` once the codec pads the month.

exports.name: cardDigits
exports.description: Digits only — the canonical card number.

exports.name: cardExpiryCodec
exports.description:
Card expiry typed as digits: `"7"` → `"07"` (a month above 1 cannot take a
second digit), `"0729"` → `"07/29"`. Canonical and display are both `MM/YY`.

exports.name: cardNumberCodec
exports.description: Card number: shown grouped, stored as digits capped at the brand's length.

exports.name: cardNumberMask
exports.description:
The number's input mask for `useMask` (`@kitora/primitives`), chosen by the leading digits: the brand's
groups (Amex 4-6-5), one `9` per digit and a space between groups. It lays digits out exactly as
{@link formatCardNumber} does, so the codec stays the one source of the grouping; the mask adds the caret.

exports.name: detectCardBrand
exports.description: The brand the leading digits indicate (`unknown` when none matches yet).

exports.name: formatCardNumber
exports.description: Display form: digits grouped per brand (`3782 822463 10005`), capped at the brand's length.

exports.name: isExpired
exports.description: A card is valid through the LAST day of its expiry month; expired from the first day of the next.

exports.name: luhnValid
exports.description: Luhn (mod 10) check over the digits; numbers shorter than {@link MIN_PAN_LENGTH} fail.

exports.name: parseExpiry
exports.description: `"MM/YY"` (or `"MM/YYYY"`, or a `{ month, year }`) → numbers; `null` when malformed or month out of range.

exports.name: CardBrand
exports.description: A card brand the number field recognises, or `unknown` (see {@link CARD_BRANDS}).

exports.name: CardExpiry
exports.description: A card expiry as numbers (`year` is four digits).

exports.name: TextCodec
exports.description: A display ⇄ canonical text codec (same shape as the model registry's `CodecDef` and the fields' `Codec<string>`).

exports.name: compareTime
exports.description: Negative when `a` is earlier than `b`; malformed values sort first.

exports.name: detectTimeZone
exports.description: The runtime's zone (`Intl` resolved), `"UTC"` when it cannot tell.

exports.name: formatTime
exports.description: Display a canonical time: `"1:30 PM"` in 12-hour mode, the canonical string in 24-hour mode. `""` when malformed.

exports.name: isTimeZone
exports.description: Whether `zone` is an IANA zone this runtime accepts.

exports.name: dateTimeValue
exports.description:
Any date-time a `DateTimeField` has stored (RFC 9557, an instant with `Z`, the offset form saved before value kinds,
or a wall time read in `zone`) → the same instant in the `valueKind` shape, in `zone`; `undefined` when unparseable.
Use it to migrate stored values, on the server or the client: `dateTimeValue("2026-07-01T09:30:00-04:00",
"America/New_York")` is `"2026-07-01T09:30:00-04:00[America/New_York]"`.
exports.signature: (value: string, zone: string, valueKind?: DateTimeValueKind) => string | undefined

exports.name: DATE_TIME_VALUE_KINDS
exports.description: How a `DateTimeField` stores its value: the pickers DatePicker's `zoned` and `instant` value kinds.

exports.name: joinZoned
exports.description:
Wall date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) + time (`HH:mm`) in `zone` → an ISO instant with the
zone's offset at that moment (DST-aware). `undefined` when either part is
missing or malformed. The pickers zone core resolves DST with Temporal's
`"compatible"` rule: a time a spring-forward gap skips moves forward by the
gap (02:30 on the New York change day is stored as `03:30:00-04:00`), a
repeated fall-back time takes the earlier instant.
exports.signature: (date: string, time: string, zone: string) => string | undefined

exports.name: listTimeZones
exports.description: Every IANA zone the runtime knows, sorted by offset then name, offsets taken at `at`.

exports.name: parseTime
exports.description: `"HH:mm"` / `"HH:mm:ss"` → parts; `null` when malformed or out of range.

exports.name: prefersHour12
exports.description: Whether the locale writes times on a 12-hour clock (en-US yes, en-GB / de no).

exports.name: splitZoned
exports.description: An ISO instant (offset or `Z`, or RFC 9557 with a zone) → the wall date and time it shows in `zone`; `undefined` when unparseable.
exports.signature: (iso: string, zone: string) => { date: string; time: string; } | undefined

exports.name: timeSlots
exports.description: Every `step`-minute slot of the day from `min` to `max` inclusive, canonical strings (the time picker's list).
exports.signature: (stepMinutes: number, min?: string, max?: string) => string[]

exports.name: timeString
exports.description: Canonical `"HH:mm"` (seconds only when non-zero or `withSeconds`).

exports.name: timeToSeconds
exports.description: Seconds since midnight, for ordering and step math.

exports.name: timeZoneOffsetMinutes
exports.description: Offset of `zone` from UTC at `instant`, in minutes (`+330` for Asia/Kolkata). Throws on an unknown zone. The pickers zone core's `offsetMinutesAt`.

exports.name: DateTimeValueKind
exports.description: How a `DateTimeField` stores its value: `zoned` (RFC 9557 with the zone) or `instant` (UTC with `Z`).

exports.name: TimeParts
exports.description: A parsed time of day.

exports.name: TimeZoneEntry
exports.description: One IANA zone with its current offset, for the timezone picker.

exports.name: matrixAnswered
exports.description: Rows of `rows` that have an answer (a non-empty string or a non-empty list).
exports.signature: (value: MatrixValue | undefined, rows: readonly string[]) => number

exports.name: PERMISSION_STATES
exports.description: Tri-state of a header checkbox: every covered cell has every action, none has any, or a mix.

exports.name: permissionCellState
exports.description: Header state over the cells `roles × resources` for `actions`.
exports.signature: (v: PermissionValue, roles: readonly string[], resources: readonly string[], actions: readonly string[]) => PermissionState

exports.name: setPermissionColumn
exports.description: Grant (`on`) or revoke every action on one resource for every role.
exports.signature: (v: PermissionValue, roles: readonly string[], resource: string, actions: readonly string[], on: boolean) => PermissionValue

exports.name: setPermissionRow
exports.description: Grant (`on`) or revoke every action on every resource of one role.
exports.signature: (v: PermissionValue, role: string, resources: readonly string[], actions: readonly string[], on: boolean) => PermissionValue

exports.name: togglePermission
exports.description: Add or remove one action on one (role, resource) cell. `order` (the field's actions) keeps a stable order.
exports.signature: (v: PermissionValue, role: string, resource: string, action: string, order?: readonly string[]) => PermissionValue

exports.name: MatrixAnswer
exports.description: One matrix answer: a single column value or, in multi mode, the chosen column values.

exports.name: MatrixRowsArgs
exports.description: `matrixRows` validator argument: which rows exist, and `"all"` or a minimum count that must be answered.

exports.name: MatrixValue
exports.description: A matrix field's value: each row key mapped to its answer (absent while unanswered).

exports.name: PermissionState
exports.description: A header checkbox's tri-state: `all`, `none` or `mixed` (see {@link PERMISSION_STATES}).

exports.name: PermissionValue
exports.description: A permission matrix's value: role → resource → granted actions, in the order of the field's `actions` list.

exports.name: isRichTextDoc
exports.description: Is `v` a JSON rich-text document (`{ type: "doc", … }`)? The guard every helper narrows with.

exports.name: isRichTextEmpty
exports.description:
Empty for `required`: no visible text. An editor's "empty" document is
`{ type: "doc", content: [{ type: "paragraph" }] }` — an object, so the
generic empty check would call it filled. RichTextField stores `null` for
such a document; this is the same test for values that arrive from elsewhere.

`value` under `name` (the resolved dot path). `native: true` means the
control itself carries the `name` (a text input), so hidden inputs are only
rendered when it is swapped for the read-only view (`readOnlyIf` is
"shown, still sent"). Otherwise (custom controls: select, checkbox, date,
codec…) hidden inputs always carry the value. A hidden field posts nothing.

props.name: group

matrix…): the field renders as `<fieldset>` + `<legend>` (the legend names
every input inside), and the fieldset carries `aria-describedby` for the
description/error. `htmlFor` then becomes the fieldset id.

exports.name: AsyncOnStale
exports.description:
N11 — what happens to a saved value that a SETTLED, unsearched option list no
longer carries (an id from another account after the account changed):
`"keep"` leaves it (the default, the behaviour before this option), `"clear"`
empties it, `{ set }` writes a sentinel such as `"0"`. Judged only after a
successful load with no search text, never while loading or after an error,
and written as a user edit, so the field turns dirty.

`view={views.commaList()}` on a multi-select stored as `"pos,web"`, or
`view={views.choice({ yes: true, no: false })}` on a radio stored as a boolean
(`views` in fields/views.ts). Dirty and the payload keep the stored shape.

props.name: visibleIf
props.description: Model rules — evaluated in the core, so the field hides/validates the same on a server.

props.name: disabledIf
props.description: Model condition under which the field is disabled (see `whenDisabled` for the payload).

props.name: readOnlyIf
props.description: Model condition under which the field shows its static value; it is still sent.

props.name: whenHidden
props.description: What happens to the stored value when the field becomes inactive: `clear`, `keep` or `keep-and-send` (the model's default is `clear`).

props.name: rules
props.description: Validators run in the core; a failure is an error that blocks submit.

props.name: warn
props.description: Validators whose failures show as warnings; they do not block submit.

props.name: default
props.description: Seeded when the field becomes active with no value.

props.name: local
props.description: Local/UI-only: validated, never sent.

props.name: whenDisabled
props.description: N6 — `"send"`: a disabled field (`disabledIf`) is still sent with its value; default `"omit"`.

props.name: inherit
props.description:

non-empty wins (`[e.ref("base.label"), e.ctx("global.label")]`). Text fields show the
inherited value as their placeholder; `SwitchField tristate` shows it while unset.
The value itself stays empty (and `emptyPolicy: "omit"` keeps it out of the payload).

exports.name: plural
exports.description:
Pick the right plural form for `count` in `locale` (CLDR rules via
Intl.PluralRules). `forms` must at least provide `other`; `{n}` in the chosen
form is replaced with the count. An unknown locale falls back to `other`.

  plural(1, { one: "{n} error", other: "{n} errors" })  // "1 error"
  plural(3, { one: "{n} error", other: "{n} errors" })  // "3 errors"
exports.signature: (count: number, forms: PluralForms, locale?: string) => string

exports.name: PluralCategory
exports.description: One CLDR plural category: `zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many` or `other`.

exports.name: WIZARD_SUMMARY_CLASS
exports.description:
The review summary styled as one bordered block per step: a header line with the step name and
its Edit link, then a two-column label/value list. Styles target the headless markup
(`section > h3 > button`, `dl > div > dt + dd`), so the summary's behaviour stays react/'s.

exports.name: WizardNav
exports.description:
Back / Next, and `Form.Submit` on the last step (legacy wizards: a completing button). All three share the default button height.
While a step commit runs (`onStepComplete`) Next is busy and both buttons are disabled; a failed commit shows its message
under the buttons (`useWizard().stepError`), so a per-step save needs no route glue.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes merged onto the button row.

props.name: disableUntilComplete
props.description: Whether Next (and the last step's submit) stay disabled until the step is complete, silently (`useWizard().stepComplete`).

props.name: skip
props.description: Gap K — show Skip, which moves on without validating the step (`useWizard().skip()`); `true` for the default label, or the label itself.

exports.name: WizardProgress
exports.description:
Numbered progress list; completed steps (passed in this session, or recorded by the server
through `<Wizard completed>`, G7) show a check mark, reachable steps are buttons (forward too,
once every earlier step is complete), the current one is marked `aria-current="step"`. Below
`sm` only the current step keeps its label (the others stay as numbered dots) so a 4-step list
fits a 390px phone without sideways scroll.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes merged onto the list.

exports.name: WizardSummary
exports.description:
Styled `<Wizard.Summary>`; `className` merges after {@link WIZARD_SUMMARY_CLASS}. A caller
`format` never sees a filled password / `sensitive` row: those always render {@link SUMMARY_MASK},
so a value formatter (dates, currency) cannot leak a secret onto the review step by accident.

exports.name: MultiSelectField
exports.description:
Many values from a static list. Chips in the trigger (each removable with
its × button); the popup (a bottom sheet below `md`) is the collections
kit's multiple-selection `Listbox`. Keys: ArrowDown/Enter/Space on the
trigger opens; in the list ↑/↓/Home/End and typeahead move, Space/Enter
toggle, Shift+↑/↓ extend, Ctrl/Cmd+A toggles all, Escape closes and returns
focus to the trigger.

exports.name: AsyncMultiOnStale
exports.description:
N11 — the multi-select twin of `AsyncSelectField`'s `onStale`: what happens to
saved values the option list no longer carries (ids from another account after
the account changed). `"keep"` leaves them (the default, the behaviour before
this option), `"clear"` drops only the missing ones and keeps the rest, `{ set }`
replaces the whole value with a sentinel list when any is missing. Judged only
on a successful load with no search text and no further page (`hasMore` false,
so absence is proven), never while loading or after an error; written as a
user edit, so the field turns dirty.

exports.name: PermissionMatrixField

each holding one narrow column per action (the action names appear once, in a
second header row, so three roles × three actions fit a ~500px column). Row headers grant/revoke every
action of a resource for every role; column headers do the same for a
role across resources; both are tri-state (all / none / mixed).

of a flat GraphQL input, or a single-value modal (`pick={["webhookUrl"]}`).

exports.name: RowSubFormDialog
exports.description:
G3 inside a repeater: a sub-form over the ROW (or any scope) this dialog
renders in — a per-row "manual access" modal that edits the row in a scratch
store and, on Complete, writes the row plus `set` back as ONE undo step and
ONE change event. Render it inside the row (a `<FieldArray>` row template):
the row's path comes from the render scope, and the parent store from the
`<Form>` around it. `Row` types `empty`, `set` and the seed (a runtime path
cannot be typed, so the row's shape is the caller's claim, like a FieldArray
row type). Cancel leaves the row untouched.

props.description: Starting values when the scope holds no object (normally never: a row always has one).

props.description: Extra config of the scratch store (`model`, `persist` draft…).

props.name: set
props.description: Extra writes in the same commit, paths RELATIVE to the row: `() => [{ path: "granted", value: true }]`.

props.name: onCommit
props.description: Called after the row was written.

props.name: rowContext
props.description: App context for the dialog's rules, read from the row at open: `(row) => ({ channel: row.channel })`.

exports.name: SubFormDialog
exports.description:
A FormDialog over a slice of a parent form (G3): each open seeds a scratch
store from the parent at `scope`; it can hold its own `<Wizard>` (pass
`submit={false}` so the wizard's last step is the only finish); submitting
writes the slice plus `set` into the parent as ONE undo step and ONE change
event; Cancel (or the discard guard) leaves the parent untouched.

props.name: parent
props.description: The parent form whose slice this dialog edits.

props.name: scope
props.description: The parent path edited; its current value seeds each open.

props.name: empty
props.description: Starting values when the parent has nothing at `scope` yet.

props.name: form
props.description: Extra config of the scratch store (rules come from the JSX inside; `model`, `persist` draft…).

props.name: set
props.description: Extra parent writes in the same commit, e.g. `() => [{ path: "setupConfirmed", value: true }]`.

props.name: onCommit
props.description: Called after the parent was written.

props.name: onBeforeCommit
props.description:
Gap D — awaited inside the dialog's submit BEFORE the parent is written (a
mutation the modal runs before it closes). A throw keeps the dialog open with
the message in its status (a non-SubmitError is read with `mapErrors`) and
leaves the parent untouched.

props.name: parentContext
props.description:
G2 — app context for the sub-form's rules, read from the parent at open:
`(parent) => ({ tool: parent.tool })` lets the dialog's steps branch on a
parent field (`visibleIf={c.eq(e.ctx("method"), "vault")}`) without copying it into the slice.

secret on the server (`TURNSTILE_TEST_SECRETS`).

exports.name: useMediaQuery
exports.description:
`true` while the viewport matches `query`. SSR-safe by construction: the
server snapshot is always `false`, React hydrates with it and then re-renders

hydration mismatch. `false` in engines without `matchMedia` (jsdom, old WebViews).

exports.name: ArrayContext

exports.name: CellLabelContext

Inside a `layout="table"` repeater cell: the ids of
the cell's column header and its row label, space-separated, for the
control's `aria-labelledby`. The column header names the cell, so the field
renders no visible label of its own. `null` outside a table cell.

exports.name: FormContext

exports.name: FormDomContext

exports.name: fieldDomId
exports.description: DOM id for the control bound to `path` in the form with `idPrefix`. No prefix (no <Form>) → the bare path.

exports.name: findFieldElement
exports.description:
The control element for `path` inside THIS form, or null. Looks the prefixed
id up and rejects any element outside the form element, so a lookup can never
land in another form on the page.
exports.signature: (dom: FormDom | null, path: string) => HTMLElement | null

exports.name: findFocusTarget
exports.description:
The element focus-first-error moves to for `path` inside THIS form (H17):
the field's control; a non-focusable control (a group) → its first
focusable descendant, else the group itself (made programmatically
focusable, `tabindex=-1`); an array-level issue → the repeater container;
a group-level path (`address`) → the first control under it in DOM order.
exports.signature: (dom: FormDom | null, path: string) => HTMLElement | null

exports.name: ModelOnlyContext
exports.description: True inside a phantom row: fields register their model node and nothing else.

exports.name: ModelParentContext
exports.description:
Model plumbing. Every model component (field, <When>,
<Variant>, <Variant.Case>, <FieldArray>) registers a node whose parent is the
nearest enclosing registration; the store assembles the tree from these.
- `ModelParentContext` — registration id of the enclosing model component (null = root)
- `ModelScopeContext` — the enclosing <FieldArray>s and named scopes, outermost first
  (assembly rewrites scoped paths relative to them and collapses rows into one template)
- `ModelSuppressContext` — true inside a composite field (Address/Money/…): the
  composite registers ONE node; its sub-inputs bind values but add no nodes
- `ModelOnlyContext` — true inside a phantom row (an empty array still
  tells the model its row template): fields register their node and nothing
  else — no store registration, no resources, no rendering in the document
- `TemplateChainContext` — names of the enclosing <FieldTemplate>s, so a
  phantom expansion of a template inside itself stops (no infinite recursion)

exports.name: ModelScopeContext
exports.description: The enclosing `<FieldArray>`s and named scopes, outermost first (see the block above).

exports.name: ModelSuppressContext
exports.description: True inside a composite field: its sub-inputs bind values but register no model nodes.

exports.name: resolveScopedName
exports.description:
Resolve a field name against the enclosing scopes: `.x` is
relative to the nearest scope, each extra leading dot climbs one scope, `/x`
is form-absolute, anything else is already absolute.

exports.name: RowContext
exports.description: The array row being rendered (stable row id + current index), for row actions and row labels.

exports.name: ScopeContext
exports.description: The innermost value scope (see `ScopeFrame`); null at the form root.

exports.name: scopePaths
exports.description: Concrete scope paths from the root to `frame`, outermost first (the `scopes` list expressions evaluate in).

exports.name: TemplateChainContext
exports.description: Names of the enclosing `<FieldTemplate>`s, so a template nested in itself stops expanding.

exports.name: useFormStore
exports.description: The store of the enclosing `<Form>`; throws outside one, because a field with no store would silently do nothing.

exports.name: useResolvedName
exports.description: Resolve `name` against the scope this component renders in.

exports.name: FocusRegion
exports.description:
Something that owns fields which may not be in the document right now (H17):
a `<Wizard>` (fields of the other steps live in a detached container), an
`EditableGrid` (virtualized rows are not rendered). Focus-first-error asks it
where its errored paths sit and lets it do the reveal.

Ordering contract ("first" error): a region with an `anchor` takes part in
DOM order at that element's position, its own paths ordered by `rank`; a
region whose `anchor()` is null (the wizard's other steps) is DEFERRED —
considered only when no error is visible in the current view, earliest
`rank` (step order) first.

exports.name: FormDom
exports.description:
DOM identity of one rendered <Form>.

Why: field ids used to equal the field path, so two forms on one page with a
shared field name produced duplicate ids, and `document.getElementById(path)`
could focus a control in the wrong form. Each <Form> now owns a `useId()`
prefix and its <form> element; ids and focus lookups go through both.

exports.name: RowFrame
exports.description: One rendered repeater row: stable id and current index (for row-level controls such as RowActions).

exports.name: ScopeFrame
exports.description:
One enclosing value scope: a <FieldScope>, a <FieldArray> row or a
scoped <Wizard.Step>. `path` is the CONCRETE canonical prefix right now (a
row's index path is re-derived from its id on every render, so a row keeps
pointing at its own data after move/insert/remove). `parent` is the next
scope out (`null` = the form root).

exports.name: FieldScope
exports.description:
A named object scope: every relative name inside resolves under
`name`. Compiles to a `group` node, exactly what `f.group(name, …)` writes,
so a reusable sub-form (`<FieldScope name="shipping"><AddressFields /></FieldScope>`)
is the same model whichever front-end built it.

props.name: name
props.description: The object path this scope opens; itself relative-capable (`.address` inside a row).

props.name: label
props.description: Model label of the group node.

props.name: children
props.description: Fields and layout inside the scope; their relative names resolve under `name`.

exports.name: FieldTemplate
exports.description:
Render `children` as an instance of a named template (recursive
forms). Registers a `use` node where it stands; its rendered children become
the body of `templates[name]` (all instances render the same body, so the
first one that rendered any defines it). Inside a phantom row a template
already being expanded higher up renders only its `use` node — the body is
known — which is what stops a recursive template from expanding forever.

props.name: name
props.description: Template name: `templates[name]` in the model; a `use` node marks each instance.

props.name: children
props.description: The template body, rendered for this instance.

exports.name: ScopeProvider
exports.description: Provide a value scope (and, when given, a model scope) to `children`. Shared by every scope-opening component.

props.name: path
props.description: Concrete path prefix that relative names below resolve against.

props.name: model
props.description: Model scope to push for model assembly; omit to open a value scope only.

props.name: children
props.description: The subtree inside the scope.

exports.name: useScope
exports.description:
Read the enclosing scope as `S`. A reusable sub-form declares the
shape it expects; `expect` lists keys it reads, and mounting it where the
scope's value is an object missing one of them is reported loudly
(console.error), never a silent new field. `rel` gives typed relative names
(JSX children cannot be contextually typed by their parent, so this is the
typed path inside a sub-form).

props.name: name
props.description: The object path this scope opens; itself relative-capable (`.address` inside a row).

props.name: label
props.description: Model label of the group node.

props.name: children
props.description: Fields and layout inside the scope; their relative names resolve under `name`.

props.name: name
props.description: Template name: `templates[name]` in the model; a `use` node marks each instance.

props.name: children
props.description: The template body, rendered for this instance.

exports.description: The scope a component renders in, typed by the author's view of it (see {@link useScope}).

props.name: name

props.name: children

props.name: max

props.name: removeGuard

exports.name: FieldArrayRow
exports.description: A row in the render-prop API: id/index/value plus `scope(children)`, which renders children in this row's scope.

props.name: move
props.description: Up/down buttons.

props.name: remove
props.description: Whether to show the Remove button.

props.name: duplicate
props.description: Whether to show the Duplicate button (inserts a copy of the row below it).

props.description: Whether to show the Insert-below button (inserts a new row below it).

props.type: (row: { index: number; value: unknown }) => boolean | Promise<boolean>
props.description:
N5 — ask before removing a row (`useConfirm()` → "Are you sure?"): resolve `true` to
remove, `false` to keep it. Gets the row's index and current value. Remove guards
(`removeGuard`) still run after a yes; a sync guard is the place for rules, this is

exports.name: RowActionsSlot
exports.description:
A component that stands in for `<FieldArray.RowActions>` in a row template (a styled wrapper
that renders it). The array reads such a child's flags into the model (`rowActions`) and gives
it the "Actions" table column, exactly as for RowActions itself; without the marker a styled
wrapper would be invisible to both and AutoForm would lose the row controls.

props.name: rowActionsSlot
props.description: Marker the array looks for; set it to `true` on the wrapper component.

exports.name: CUSTOM_FIELD_TYPE
exports.description: Node type registered by a plain `useField` binding that names no widget type.

exports.name: shallowEqual
exports.description: Shallow value-equality for object selectors passed to {@link useFormState}.
exports.signature: <T extends Record<string, unknown>>(a: T, b: T) => boolean

exports.name: useAbandonTracking
exports.description:
Emit `abandon` when the page is hidden or unloaded while the form is dirty
and unsubmitted (analytics funnels). Opt-in: mount it once inside
`<Form>` (or pass the store).

exports.name: useArrayRow
exports.description:
Bind to one FieldArray row by its STABLE id (H7 / K2). The store resolves
id → current index on every array change, so a row component that only knows
its id always points at the right data after move/insert/remove — no index
tearing. The array path comes from the enclosing <FieldArray> (or pass it
explicitly). Subscribes to the array path; the snapshot is the index (a
primitive), so it stays ref-stable for useSyncExternalStore.

exports.name: useComputed
exports.description:
Subscribe to a computed key declared outside `T` (`defineForm<T, D>()`),
typed by the definition; re-renders when it changes. Read-only: there is no
setter for `D`'s paths. Must be inside the `<Form>` whose model is `def`.
exports.typeParameters: <T, D extends object, P extends FieldPath<D>>
exports.signature: <T, D extends object, P extends FieldPath<D>>(_def: FormDef<T, D>, path: P) => FieldValue<D, P> | undefined

exports.name: useField
exports.description:
Bind to one field. Subscribes to ONLY this path (re-renders in isolation),
registers it with the store on mount, and contributes its node to the
form's model: `visibleIf`, `requiredIf`, `rules` … run in the core.
Inside a <When>/<Variant> branch it registers as `conditional` (legacy
unmount-clears-value), and the model's `whenHidden` clears it on hide.

exports.name: useFocusRegion
exports.description:
Register a {@link FocusRegion} with the enclosing `<Form>` for focus-first-error
(H17). The region object may change every render: a stable forwarder reads the
latest one, so registration happens once per mount. `null` registers nothing.

exports.name: useForm
exports.description: Create a form store once and keep it stable across renders; optionally controlled by a host (`value` / `onChange`).
exports.typeParameters: <T extends object, TOut = T, TResult = unknown>
exports.signature: <T extends object, TOut = T, TResult = unknown>(config: UseFormConfig<T, TOut, TResult>) => FormStore<T, TOut, TResult>

exports.name: useFormErrors
exports.description:
Reactive form-level error aggregate (A8 — error summary). Re-renders on form
events so an <ErrorSummary> or submit-disabled affordance stays in sync.

exports.name: useFormHistory
exports.description: Reactive undo/redo controls. Re-renders on form events so button enablement stays in sync.

exports.name: useFormLoading
exports.description:
Is the enclosing form loading its record? `false` outside a form,
so a field rendered on its own never shows a skeleton. Re-renders only when
the load state flips.

exports.name: useFieldSave
exports.description:
One field's autosave status and a retry, for chrome that shows
"Saving…" / "Saved" / "Couldn't save · Retry". Outside a `<Form>`, or for a
field that was never saved, the state is `undefined`. Re-renders only when
that field's record changes.
exports.signature: (path: string | undefined) => { state: SaveState | undefined; retry: () => void; }

exports.name: useFieldStateFlags
exports.description:
One field's `touched`, `dirty` and `filled` flags: what the Field primitive (`@kitora/primitives`' `Field.Root`)
calls its state, and what the field shell writes as `data-touched`, `data-dirty` and `data-filled`. All `false`
outside a `<Form>` or without a path. Re-renders only when one of the three flips.
exports.signature: (path: string | undefined) => { touched: boolean; dirty: boolean; filled: boolean; }

exports.name: useFormState
exports.description:
Subscribe to a form-level aggregate slice (e.g. isValid / status / errorCount)
without re-rendering on every keystroke. The selector result is memoized by
`isEqual` (default `Object.is`) so object selectors don't tear or loop — pass
`shallowEqual` when selecting an object, e.g.
  useFormState((f) => ({ valid: f.getIssues().length === 0, submitting: f.getStatus() === "submitting" }), shallowEqual)
exports.signature: <S>(selector: (store: ReturnType<typeof useFormStore>) => S, isEqual?: (a: S, b: S) => boolean) => S

exports.name: useIsClient
exports.description:
`false` during the server render and hydration, `true` after (and from the first render of a tree that is not
hydrating): gate what needs the DOM at render (a portal host, an editor, a map, a widget script) so the server HTML
and the first client render agree.

exports.name: useIsoLayoutEffect
exports.description: `useLayoutEffect` in the browser, `useEffect` on the server (no warning, no-op there).

exports.name: useModelNode
exports.description:
Register the model node a component contributes and return its
registration id (children use it as their parent). `null` registers nothing.

Registration runs in a layout effect, so a whole tree registers inside one
commit and `<Form>` rebuilds the model once, before paint. A changed entry
updates in place (its position among siblings is kept). Inside a composite
field ({@link ModelSuppressContext}) nothing is registered.

exports.name: useNavigationGuard
exports.description:
Dirty-guard on navigate (B7). Installs a `beforeunload` prompt while the form
is dirty (or while `when` is true) so a tab-close / reload warns about unsaved
changes. For in-app TanStack Router navigation, pair with the router's
`useBlocker({ condition })` — pass `useNavigationGuard`'s reactive dirtiness.

exports.name: useValue
exports.description: Subscribe to one path's value WITHOUT registering a field (for components that only read). Relative paths (`.x`) resolve against the enclosing scope.

exports.name: VALUES_COMPARE
exports.description: `values` change detection; canonical list.

exports.name: VIEW_CANCEL
exports.description: What a view's `set` resolves to when the change should not happen (a modal it opened was cancelled).

exports.name: ArrayRowApi
exports.description: What `useArrayRow` returns: one array row's current index and helpers keyed by its stable id.

exports.name: CondObject
exports.description: A condition given as an expression object (a string `required` is a message, not a condition).

exports.name: ConfirmChange
exports.description:
G1 — a gate on USER changes: return true to apply `next`, false to drop it,
or a promise (a confirm dialog) that decides later. Programmatic, external
and model writes (`setValue` from code, `rebase`, effects) never pass
through it, and the value is not written (nor autosaved) until it resolves true.

exports.name: FieldApi
exports.description: What `useField` returns: one field's live state and the handlers that change it.

exports.name: FieldView
exports.description:
Gap E — a field-edge lens between the STORED
value (the wire shape the store keeps, dirties and serializes) and the value the
CONTROL works on. `get(stored)` is what the control shows; `set(control, prev)`
is what the store writes for a user edit — or a promise of it (a modal that asks
for the value), or {@link VIEW_CANCEL} to write nothing. Examples: a multi-select
over a comma-joined string, a radio of booleans, a switch over a non-boolean.
Values are `unknown` on purpose: one field's lens is chosen by its caller, and
each helper (`views.*` in fields/) narrows at runtime.

exports.name: decodeFormData
exports.description:
Decode a posted `FormData` into the nested value a form holds.

- Paths: `items.0.qty`, `items[0].qty`, `items[].qty` (append order), `m['k']`.
- Without a definition every value stays a string (files stay `File`s); a
  repeated key becomes a list.
- With a definition each leaf is coerced by its node's widget type (numbers,
  booleans — absent → `false`, lists — absent → `[]`), and keys the
  definition does not declare are dropped.
- Reserved keys (`$intent`, `$ACTION_*`) are skipped; read `$intent` with `formIntent`.
exports.signature: (formData: FormData, def?: FormDef, opts?: DecodeOptions) => Record<string, unknown>

exports.name: RESERVED_KEY_PREFIX
exports.description: A posted key starting with this is reserved (`$intent`, React's `$ACTION_*` fields), never a value.

exports.name: DecodeDropReason

exports.name: DecodeOptions

{@link FormState} that `useForm({ serverState })` merges on the client.

Invariant: the handler runs only for a valid post, never for an intent.

exports.description: Options of the OpenAPI source: the JSON Schema options plus which operation's request body becomes the form.

exports.name: GRAPHQL_ERROR_SOURCES
exports.description: Both example GraphQL conventions: resolver errors with `extensions.field` first, then mutation `userErrors`.

exports.name: graphQLErrorsSource
exports.description:
Top-level GraphQL `errors[]`. The field comes from `extensions.field`
(string or segments), then `extensions.path`; the response `path` names a
RESPONSE field (`["sharingUpdate"]`), so it is not used — an error without
an explicit field is form-level. `extensions.code` becomes the code.

exports.name: submitErrorFromGraphQL
exports.description: {@link mapErrors} with {@link GRAPHQL_ERROR_SOURCES} — for a backend that follows those conventions.
exports.signature: <T = unknown>(input: unknown, opts?: Omit<MapErrorsOptions<T>, "sources">) => SubmitError<T> | undefined

exports.name: INPUT_ARG_SEGMENTS
exports.description:
Leading segments of a `userErrors[].field` that name the mutation's input
argument, not a form field (e.g. `["input", "title"]`). Dropped before
the path map sees the name.

exports.name: userErrorFieldName
exports.description: A field named as a string or a segment list, input-argument prefix dropped.

exports.name: userErrorsSource
exports.description:
Mutation payload `userErrors: [{ field: string[] | null, message, code }]`.
Accepts the response, its `data`, a mutation payload, or a client error
carrying the response. An empty list is a recognised success (`[]`), not
"unknown shape".
